title: [Suggestion] Add minimum Behavior Quality filter to matchmaking
body: ## Description Please add an optional matchmaking setting that allows players to specify the **minimum Behavior Quality** they are willing to accept. Dota Plus already evaluates the Behavior Quality of a match before the player accepts it. However, there is currently no way to tell the matchmaker to continue searching when the predicted behavior quality is below the player's preference. ## Current Problem A matchmaking search can take **5-10 minutes**. When a match is finally found, it may show **Disruptive** behavior. If the player doesn't want to accept that match, the current process becomes: > **Queue -> wait 5-10 minutes -> Disruptive Behavior -> decline -> queue again** This can repeat several times. In my experience, roughly **4 out of 5 matches found** can have Disruptive Behavior. The frustrating part is that the matchmaking system already knows the Behavior Quality before presenting the match. Instead of requiring the player to manually decline and restart the search, it should be possible to tell the matchmaker to continue searching automatically. ## Suggested Solution Add a matchmaking preference such as: **Minimum Behavior Quality:** - Any - Acceptable or better - Good or better - Very Good For example: > **Minimum Behavior Quality: Good or better** > > ⚠️ Higher behavior requirements may significantly increase matchmaking time. If I select **Good or better**, the matchmaker should simply continue searching when it finds a lobby below that threshold instead of presenting it to me. I am completely fine with a longer queue. I would rather wait **30-40 minutes continuously** for a suitable match than repeatedly wait 5-10 minutes, decline a Disruptive Behavior match, and restart the queue. ## Optional Setting - No Impact on Players Who Want Faster Queues This should be entirely optional. The default could remain: > **Minimum Behavior Quality: Any** Players who prioritize queue speed would experience no change. Players who care more about Behavior Quality could voluntarily accept longer matchmaking times. ## Why This Would Help - Eliminates repeated manual declining and requeueing. - Gives players more control over the tradeoff between **queue time and Behavior Quality**. - Makes maintaining a high Behavior Score more meaningful. - Gives players with poor behavior an additional incentive to improve. - Does not negatively affect players who prefer faster matchmaking because the filter would be optional. Dota Plus already provides this information before a match is accepted. **Please allow players to use the same information as a matchmaking preference.**

title: Critical Bug: Behavior Score Database Overwrite / Summary Row Rollback After a Single Match
body: Dear Dota 2 Development Team / Steam Support, I am writing to report a critical database synchronization bug within the Conduct Summary system. A newly generated summary row was completely overwritten and rolled back in real-time by a subsequent match server, resulting in an erroneous, instant loss of 1,000 Behavior Score (BS) points, a 24-hour matchmaking ban, and Low Priority status. Account and Match Context (Timeline of the Bug on October 3rd, 2026): 1. The Correct Update: I finished a 15-game block. At 09:33 GMT, Conduct Summary #9027024387 was initially generated. My score increased by roughly +341 points from the previous 1954 BS, correctly displaying 2295 BS in my profile. 2. The Overwrite Trigger: Immediately after, I joined a new match as Phantom Assassin (PA). This match suffered from severe server-side lag and ping spikes (up to 150ms). I did not disconnect, did not abandon, and completed the match normally. 3. The Rollback Error: Instantly upon returning to the main menu after the PA match, the system did not create a new log entry. Instead, it retroactively modified the already generated Summary #9027024387. The final Behavior Score value was altered from 2295 to 1297, while leaving the game metrics completely clean (0 reports, 0 abandons). Full Account Historical Data (Proof of Contradiction): Here is the exact data extracted from my personal game logs, demonstrating that a perfect 15-game block resulted in a massive score drop due to the overwrite: MatchID Date (GMT) Periodic Ex.Reports Ex.Abandons MatchCount Positive Reported Abandoned Reports Commends BehaviorScore [BEFORE THE PA MATCH - ORIGINAL RECORD (Captured at 08:13:46 GMT)] MatchID Date (GMT) Periodic Ex.Reports Ex.Abandons MatchCount Positive Reported Abandoned Reports Commends BehaviorScore 9027024387 2026-10-03 08:13:46 Yes No No 15 15 0 0 0 35 2297 [AFTER THE PA MATCH - OVERWRITTEN RECORD (Captured at 09:33:47 GMT)] MatchID Date (GMT) Periodic Ex.Reports Ex.Abandons MatchCount Positive Reported Abandoned Reports Commends BehaviorScore 9027024387 2026-10-03 09:33:47 Yes No No 15 15 0 0 0 35 1297 <-- [CRITICAL DATABASE OVERWRITE BUG] [HISTORICAL DATA FOR REFERENCE] 9024012628 2026-10-01 06:55:59 Yes No No 15 15 0 0 0 29 1954 9020140670 2026-09-28 12:18:32 No Yes No 15 14 1 0 2 30 1804 9016058521 2026-09-25 20:58:18 Yes No No 15 13 2 0 6 31 2654 9013653323 2026-09-24 10:20:11 Yes No No 15 15 0 0 0 38 2404 This is an evident write-conflict / race condition between the primary behavior score calculation service and the individual match-ending script. The laggy PA match server likely fetched an outdated cached state of my account (prior to the 09:33 summary generation), processed an automated penalty state or desync error, and blindly pushed a flat -1000 point correction that forced a rewrite of the row 9027024387 instead of appending to the database correctly. Please review my account's backend transaction logs for October 3rd, 2026, specifically looking for the state collision right after the Phantom Assassin match. Please restore my score to its rightful 2295 BS. Thank you.

title: Behavior score: reports appear to outweigh commends in low-behavior brackets, creating unrecoverable loop for muted high-winrate players
body: Summary The Dota 2 behavior score system appears to have a systemic issue in low-behavior brackets: reports seem to carry disproportionate weight compared to commends. For players whose communication is already muted, this creates a loop where playing well and winning leads to enemy reports, which keeps the behavior score low and prevents recovery. Environment Game: Dota 2 Platform: Steam, PC Account ID: unsoftiz Steam ID: unsoftiz Behavior score: ~1500 (now), ~2500 (before) Duration: ~1-2 years Communication status: muted by system Winrate over period: 50-60%+ Matches played trying to recover: about 500-800+ Steps to reproduce Have a low behavior score (~1500) and muted communication. Play ranked matches and perform well (win lane, carry, high winrate). Win games or lose close games. Observe reports from enemy team (when winning) and teammates (when losing). Check behavior score after multiple games with commends. Expected behavior Commends should offset reports enough to allow recovery. Reports should be validated or weighted based on context. Muted players should not be punished for chat they cannot use. Playing well and winning should not trigger a net negative behavior score. Actual behavior Behavior score remains low or decreases. Reports appear to have near-100% success rate in low-behavior brackets. Commends do not seem to offset even a single report. Creates an endless loop: low score → reports weighted heavily → low score. Impact Dedicated players who want to play competitively are locked out of ranked matchmaking for years. The system was designed to punish toxic behavior, but it appears to punish performance and winning in low-behavior pools. Additional context I have spent thousands of hours and around $150 on this account. I want to grind to Immortal, but the behavior algorithm has blocked ranked matchmaking. I can provide match IDs, behavior score history, and screenshots for review. Request Please have the Dota team investigate how automated reports are weighted in low-behavior brackets, especially for players with muted communication and high winrates. If this is not the correct GitHub repo, please point me to the official issue tracker. If you need more information (match IDs, screenshots, etc.), let me know. Thanks.

title: Behavior Score dropped from 7,249 to 3,300 in 12 days because of Overwatch convictions for ordinary lost games. No way to appeal. 4,227 hours played, I quit today.
body: Hello Valve / Dota 2 team, My in-game name is Panda (Account ID: 194492658). I have played Dota 2 for 4,227 hours. Today, October 1, 2026, I uninstalled the game and made the decision to stop playing. I want to explain exactly why, with data, because I believe the current Behavior Score and Overwatch system is broken for solo players like me. ## What happened Over the last month I received around seven Overwatch convictions, two of them on the same day (September 20). Each one cost me roughly 1,000 Behavior Score points and sent me to Low Priority. This is the data from my own Personal Game Data page (Conduct Summary): | Summary date (GMT) | Reported matches | Reports | Commends | Behavior Score | Change | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | Sep 19, 15:04 | 0 | 0 | 29 | 7,249 | — | | Sep 20, 10:33 | 2 | 5 | 25 | 6,561 | −688 | | Sep 20, 21:49 | 3 | 6 | 24 | 5,548 | −1,013 | | Sep 21, 21:34 | 1 | 2 | 27 | 5,295 | −253 | | Sep 23, 10:32 | 3 | 7 | 23 | 5,270 | −25 | | Sep 23, 14:16 | 3 | 7 | 27 | 4,345 | −925 | | Sep 30, 08:10 | 2 | 4 | 25 | 4,238 | −107 | | Oct 1, 10:17 | 3 | 8 | 28 | 3,300 | −938 | Some things this table shows clearly: - In every single summary, 12 to 15 of my 15 matches were positive. The problem is 1–3 lost games out of every 15. - I received 23–29 commends in every summary. Most of my teammates were fine playing with me. - I received only ONE communication report in this whole period. I was not flaming or toxic in chat. These are gameplay reports from lost games. - Almost the entire 3,949-point drop comes from four large penalties of roughly −700 to −1,000 each. ## The matches **Match 9008909843 (Sep 20) — Wraith King, 3/6/9, lost.** Three of my teammates were in one party (Spirit Breaker, Lina, Templar Assassin). I had the second-highest hero damage on my team (13.2k) and died less than three of my teammates. The Templar Assassin from that party went 1/4/5 with the lowest hero damage on the team (5.0k). After this game I got an Overwatch penalty, Low Priority, and the next summary took −1,013 from me. **Match 9007822317 (Sep 20) — Dragon Knight, 2/11/13, lost.** I will be honest: this was a bad game for me. But I played until the end. I did not go AFK, I did not feed on purpose, I did not destroy items, I did not abandon. A bad game is not griefing. I was still convicted and sent to Low Priority, the second time that same day. **Match 9012524823 (Sep 23) — Wraith King, 7/15/7, lost.** Yes, I died a lot. But I also had the second-highest hero damage (25.1k) and the highest tower damage (1.9k) on my team. Again: −925. **Match 9024164970 (Oct 1) — Wraith King, 4/12/14, lost.** My last game before quitting. Our team was ahead by up to 6k net worth until about minute 27, then we lost the game in late fights. I had 30.7k hero damage, second on my team. Our support died 17 times. At the same time, in my games I regularly see teammates who stand AFK, destroy their items, build a Rapier and lose it to the enemy, or move items around to troll. As far as I can see, nothing happens to them. ## Why this system feels completely unfair 1. **There is no appeal.** Steam Support says it does not review or remove Overwatch restrictions. There is no other channel. One click from a few random players plus a quick review can take 1,000 points from a 4,000-hour player, and there is nothing I can do about it. 2. **I am never told which match I was convicted for, or why.** The notification only says "a match you recently played". I have to guess from when my Low Priority games started. How am I supposed to "improve my behavior" if I am not told what the behavior was? 3. **Bad play is punished like griefing.** I play offlane, often alone against two heroes. Dying several times early in a solo lane looks like "feeding" in a short replay fragment, but it is just Dota. Losing a lane is not a crime. 4. **Party stacks have too much power against solo players.** A group that is losing can easily push a solo player into Overwatch. 5. **It is a death spiral.** The lower my score, the worse my teammates, the more often games collapse, the more reports I get, the lower my score. Once you fall, the system pushes you further down. 6. **The punishment and the recovery are completely out of proportion.** One conviction costs about 1,000 points. A clean game gives about 10–13 points. That means one conviction erases 80–100 clean games. To get back to where I was just 12 days ago, I would need 300–400 games with ZERO reports, which is 250–330 hours of playing with one thought in my head: "please, nobody press report". ## How this makes me feel Honestly, I am angry and exhausted. I feel helpless. I have spent thousands of hours on this game because I loved it, and now every match feels like an exam where four strangers decide whether I lose a week of progress. I cannot enjoy a game where I have to play not to win, but to avoid making anyone upset after a loss. That is not Dota anymore. The joy is completely gone. ## About money Over the years I have regularly spent money on Dota 2. I supported the game because I believed in it. As of today, that is over. I will not spend anything more on Dota 2 while the behavior system works like this. ## What I am asking for 1. **A real appeal process** for Overwatch convictions, with a human review on request. 2. **Transparency:** tell the player which match they were convicted for and which behavior was the reason. 3. **A clear line between "bad game" and "griefing".** Deaths alone, or losing a lane, should not be enough for a conviction. 4. **Full context for Overwatch reviewers**, not a short fragment of the match. 5. **Accountability for reviewers** who vote "guilty" on almost every case without real review. 6. **Less weight for reports from party stacks against solo players**, and the Avoid Party protection in all modes. 7. **Proportional recovery**, so one bad week does not take hundreds of hours to fix. 8. If possible, please review my account and my recent convictions. I am writing this not just for myself, but because I see many players with exactly the same story. Please fix this system. Right now it is pushing long-time players out of the game. Thank you for reading, Panda

title: Feedback on Dota 2 Communication Score and Report System- Abuse and Harm to Regular Players
body: ### Description Hello. I have been playing Dota 2 for a long time, and I am writing not to dispute a ban or complain about a specific match. I want to draw attention to a problem in the Communication Score and report system that, in my view, harms the game and punishes innocent players. I agree that Behavior Score is a working and necessary thing. It genuinely restrains those who ruin games: AFK players, feeders, people who intentionally spoil the match. But Communication Score works differently, and here is the fundamental problem. Dota 2 is a team game where communication is critical. When a player is forcibly deprived of the ability to write and speak, it is not only he who suffers, but also his four teammates. You cannot call missing, you cannot warn about a gank, you cannot call for Roshan, you cannot coordinate a push. So the punishment of one person turns into a punishment for the entire team. At the same time, the game already has a mute button. Any player can mute any teammate or opponent and no longer see or hear them. It turns out that the forced silence system duplicates a function that every player already has, but does it for everyone at once, without their consent. A separate problem is the mechanism of reports for communication itself. It does not analyze what exactly a person wrote or said. A report triggers based on the number of complaints. Because of this, a "communication report" easily turns into a tool of revenge: a person can be reported for bad play, for an incomprehensible move, for disagreeing with someone's decision- and he will receive a silence, even though he insulted no one. This has been discussed in the community for a long time, including by well-known players and streamers. Dendi publicly said that the report system "just doesn't work"; Stray228 compared forced mute in a team game to a situation where a footballer is left on the field but forbidden to pass. So on paper, the idea of separating "behavior" and "communication" looks logical. The problem is in the execution: the system triggers too easily on false complaints and gives a normal player almost no opportunity to prove that he did nothing wrong. What, in my opinion, should be changed: 1)Remove the forced global mute, or at least make it "off by default," so that teammates can decide for themselves whether to hear this player or not. 2)Make it so that a communication report triggers only with real analysis of text or voice, and not based on the number of complaints. 3)Leave players under silence with basic pings and the chat wheel- they are not toxicity and are needed for the game. 4)Return reports to their original meaning: to punish for ruining the game, not for an "unpleasant manner of communication." I understand that this is not a technical support issue, but I ask you to forward this to the Dota 2 team. Thank you for the game and for actually reading feedback. Sincerely, Mant1cora, ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) _No response_ ### Screenshots _No response_

title: Overwatch conviction with no way for the affected player to review or challenge the decision
body: ### Description Hello Valve / Dota 2 Team, I am reporting a problem with the current Overwatch and behavior restriction system and, more specifically, the lack of transparency or an appeal/review mechanism for players who receive an Overwatch conviction. I have been playing Dota 2 since November 4, 2012, and this account has been part of my gaming history for almost 14 years. Recently, my Behavior Score dropped from 7,987 to 3,077 in a relatively short period of time. During this period I received multiple Low Priority penalties, and my communication features were eventually disabled. The most recent penalty was particularly concerning because it was issued after an Overwatch review. The match in question is: Match ID: 9001535070 Hero: Outworld Destroyer Result: Victory Score: 23 / 4 / 15 MVP Reports: 2 Commends: 28 After contacting Steam Support, I specifically asked them to investigate what happened to my account or, if Steam Support could not investigate Overwatch decisions, to provide me with a way to contact the team responsible for reviewing them. Steam Support confirmed that the matchmaking restriction was caused by an Overwatch conviction and later confirmed that the conviction was based on this exact match (9001535070). However, Steam Support also told me that: - they do not review or remove Overwatch restrictions; - they cannot provide contact information for the Overwatch team; - and there is no alternative appeal channel they can provide. I understand that Steam Support may not have the ability to manually remove an Overwatch restriction. I am not asking for special treatment or for Valve to simply remove my penalty because I disagree with it. My concern is the lack of transparency. If an Overwatch conviction is based on a specific match, I believe the affected player should at least be able to understand what behavior was considered a violation. At the moment, I have no information about: 1. What specific behavior in match 9001535070 resulted in the conviction. 2. What category of violation was identified. 3. What part or timestamp of the replay was considered evidence. 4. Whether the conviction was reviewed by multiple reviewers or how the verdict was validated. 5. Whether there is any mechanism to challenge an incorrect Overwatch verdict. I fully understand that a good KDA, winning a match, or receiving MVP does not automatically prove that no violation occurred. I am therefore not claiming that my statistics alone prove the conviction was wrong. The problem is that I have no way to determine what I supposedly did wrong in the first place. This is especially concerning because the affected player cannot meaningfully learn from or challenge a decision when the only information provided is that an Overwatch conviction occurred. There is also an important context regarding my recent Behavior Score history. Between two of my recent conduct summaries, my Behavior Score changed from 3,902 to 3,077. During those seven matches I won 6 out of 7 games. The final match in that sequence was the Outworld Destroyer game mentioned above, which was a 23/4/15 victory with 28 commends and 2 reports. Again, I am not presenting this as proof that the Overwatch verdict must be wrong. I am providing it because the circumstances make it particularly important for me to understand what behavior was actually reviewed and why it resulted in a conviction. I am also a long-time Dota 2 streamer and content creator. Because I regularly stream my games, I have experienced situations where viewers or other players intentionally watch the stream and interact with the game around it. I cannot prove that this caused the reports or the Overwatch conviction, so I am not presenting it as a fact. However, I believe it is a relevant possibility when investigating unusual reporting patterns on a streaming account. I am not asking Valve to reveal the identities of Overwatch reviewers or any private information about them. I am asking for a reasonable way for an affected player to understand and, when appropriate, challenge an Overwatch decision. My questions to the Dota 2 team are therefore: - Is there currently any way for a player to obtain information about the specific violation that resulted in an Overwatch conviction? - Is there any mechanism for reviewing or appealing a potentially incorrect Overwatch verdict? - How does Valve ensure that Overwatch convictions are sufficiently validated before they result in matchmaking restrictions and major Behavior Score penalties? - If a conviction is found to be incorrect, is there any mechanism to correct the resulting Behavior Score or other penalties? I have been playing Dota 2 for almost 14 years and I genuinely do not want to leave the game because of a punishment that I cannot understand or challenge. I would appreciate it if the Dota 2 team could clarify how this system is intended to work from the perspective of the player receiving the conviction. Thank you. ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) 9001535070 ### Screenshots

title: [VAC BUG] Unable to reconnect after crash when Dota 2 was launched from a manually created shortcut
body: ### Description ### Description I encountered a VAC-related issue that prevented me from reconnecting to an ongoing ranked match after Dota 2 crashed. Some time ago, I accidentally deleted the normal Dota 2 desktop shortcut created by Steam. Instead of recreating the standard Steam shortcut, I manually added a shortcut by browsing to the Dota 2 executable and placing that shortcut on my desktop. On September 17, 2026, I launched Dota 2 through this manually created desktop shortcut. Everything initially worked normally: - Steam was running. - Dota 2 launched normally. - I was able to search for a public ranked match. - VAC did not display any warning before matchmaking. - I connected to the match and played normally. Near the end of the match, when the game was already close to being won, Dota 2 crashed after Alt+Tab. I immediately relaunched Dota 2 and attempted to reconnect to the same match. At this point, I received the following message: "Valve Anti-Cheat was unable to verify the reliability of your device. If you do not resolve this issue, online play may be unavailable." Because of this VAC verification error, I could not reconnect to the ongoing match. I tried: - Restarting Dota 2 several times. - Restarting Steam. - Restarting my PC. - Checking my Windows security configuration. My system security configuration was: - Windows 11 64-bit - Secure Boot: Enabled - TPM version: 2.0 The issue was finally resolved when I stopped launching Dota 2 through the manually created shortcut and instead launched Dota 2 directly from my Steam Library. After launching the exact same Dota 2 installation from the Steam Library, VAC verification worked normally again. No changes were made to Windows, BIOS, TPM, Secure Boot, game files or hardware between the failed VAC verification and the successful launch from the Steam Library. ### Why this appears to be a bug The important part is that Dota 2 / VAC allowed me to: 1. Launch the game using this shortcut. 2. Enter matchmaking. 3. Accept a ranked match. 4. Connect to a VAC-secured server. 5. Play almost the entire match normally. However, after the client crashed, the same launch method caused VAC to reject the device and prevented me from reconnecting to the match. If launching Dota 2 directly through this type of shortcut is not considered valid by VAC, I believe the game should detect this before the player is allowed to enter matchmaking. Allowing the player to enter a ranked match normally and then preventing them from reconnecting after a client crash can cause an unavoidable abandon and ranked / behavior penalties. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Delete or do not use the standard Dota 2 Steam desktop shortcut. 2. Manually create a desktop shortcut by browsing to the Dota 2 executable. 3. Make sure Steam is running. 4. Launch Dota 2 using the manually created shortcut. 5. Search for and enter an online matchmaking game. 6. During the match, close or crash Dota 2. 7. Relaunch Dota 2 using the same manually created shortcut. 8. Attempt to reconnect to the match. 9. VAC may display: "Valve Anti-Cheat was unable to verify the reliability of your device." 10. Close Dota 2. 11. Launch Dota 2 directly from the Steam Library. 12. VAC verification works normally again. ### Expected behavior If Dota 2 allows a player to enter a VAC-secured ranked match, restarting the client during that match should not cause VAC to reject the same device solely because the game was launched through a different shortcut. title: System Flaw: Sub-6k communication ban empowers false-report abuse, making Behavior Score recovery mathematically impossible
body: Steam Support (Ari) directed me to post this here because the current Behavior Score system has a fundamental design flaw at the ~3k level. The way the communication ban interacts with automated reports creates an impossible, inescapable loop for players who are genuinely trying to win and improve their score. **The Core Design Flaw: Playing with Bots** Communication is the absolute core of any multiplayer team game. When you completely remove a player's ability to communicate, you turn a team-based strategic game into a single-player experience. I might as well be playing against bots, because the interaction with my team is exactly the same. When you drop below 6,000 behavior score, you cannot ask for help, coordinate with your team, ping the map effectively, or explain macro decisions. Because you cannot explain your actions, teammates lacking map awareness automatically assume you are griefing, report you, and the automated system issues severe punishments with zero human oversight. **Case Study from a Recent Match:** To demonstrate how this algorithm fails, here is exactly what happened in my recent match. I played Axe offlane with a Phoenix support against a very tough Spectre and Enchantress lane. Phoenix was role-abusing, taking farm and last hits instead of helping me survive. From a gameplay design perspective, what is the intended correct play here? - **Option A:** Stand at a safe distance on the lane, get zero gold, and leech experience from my support (who can safely solo the lane due to range and escape skills). This is widely considered griefing. - **Option B:** Leave the unplayable lane, move to the jungle to recover, and let the support have the lane. I chose Option B. I stopped contesting Phoenix for farm and went to jungle. Because I was completely muted by the system, I couldn't tell my team why I was doing this. Here is how the situation escalated: - Phoenix followed me to the jungle to steal last hits from a triple-stacked camp I made. - He/she then moved to the safe lane to stand in trees, doing nothing, but to leech XP from our carries. - He/she went in to bushes to AFK for about 15 seconds from a middle of teamfight with full hp. I ended up doing the supports (Phoenix) work, buying 3 Observers and 6 Sentries, while the actual support bought exactly 2 Sentries in a 42-minute game. I also made several immediate buybacks after dying. Again, because I was muted, I couldn't explain that this was a deliberate macro strategy. Returning to the lane meant instant death from Spectre and Enchantress. Buying back allowed me to farm safer areas and stay close to the game's overall XP progression. The scoreboard at the end of the game proves this strategy worked: I successfully kept up with the level progression and was on the exact same level as everyone else. Once I got the relevant basic items (Vanguard, Blink Dagger to counter the 4 ranged enemies, and a Blade Mail), I rotated back, tanked damage, initiated fights, and we actually won the game. I was even commended by our carries. **The Automated Punishment & The Single Draft Trap:** Despite adapting to a griefing teammate, buying the wards, playing to the very end, and winning the game, the automated system immediately hit me with a 4-hour matchmaking ban, a -500 behavior score drop, and a Low Priority penalty requiring 3 Single Draft wins to escape. This Single Draft penalty is completely contradictory and feeds directly into the same broken loop: - You are forced to play with actual, legitimate griefers who are in Low Priority for the right reasons. - Because the hero pool is restricted, teammates frequently pick unsuitable heroes for the lineup, leading to setups with 4 or 5 hard carries. - People refuse to adapt their roles, or they simply have never played the random heroes they were given. - This inevitably leads to more griefing, ruined games, and consequently, more false reports from tilted teammates. - As a result, your behavior score continues to tank even further based on false reports while you are just trying to win your 3 mandatory matches. I am a 37-year-old man, and I do not believe I have ever been a toxic player. I do not throw rage fits, and I have never abandoned a match midway through unless there was a power outage (which hasn't happened in years). I am a team player—in non-role queue games, if everyone else picks a carry or a tank, I will always try to pick a support or whatever role the team is missing. To be completely honest, I do not even remember why my behavior score originally dropped to ~3000, because it happened several years ago. Since then, due to how this communication ban and punishment loop operates, it has been practically impossible to raise it back up. **The Mathematical Impossibility:** The most broken part of this system is the math behind recovering your score: - **The Grind:** If you manage to play 15 games without a single negative ping or false report, the system updates your score by about 250 points. That is roughly 12.5 hours of playing. - **The Punishment:** After this single match—where I didn't communicate at all, adapted to a bad lane, and won the game—I lost 500 points. - **The Result:** 25 hours of clean grinding wiped out by an automated algorithm in an instant. My score dropped back to 2,500. Now, on top of a 4-hour ban and the Single Draft prison, I am forced to play AT LEAST another 25 hours of unranked games just to unlock ranked matchmaking again, just for the exact same problem to repeat. **The "For Fun" Report Exploit:** The vulnerability of this automated system is public knowledge. There are multiple YouTube videos right now showing players admitting they report others purely for fun. They proudly showcase their "Action Taken" lists on screen, openly acknowledging that none of the players they reported actually did anything wrong—yet your automated system still punishes those innocent players based on malicious reports. **Conclusion** I completely understand that a multiplayer game needs a punishment system to keep the community healthy, but this current implementation is absolutely not the right way to do it. How can a player improve their behavior score when the system mutes them from explaining legitimate gameplay decisions, forces them into an endless 25-hour grind for minimal points, traps them in Single Draft with actual griefers, and empowers those griefers to hand out automated bans? I have played Dota for 14 years, but I have completely lost faith in how this game and its automated systems are being managed. I used to absolutely hate League of Legends, but this complete lack of respect for your player base has forced me to reconsider. It has become glaringly obvious that Valve only values high-ranked and professional players, while us paying, casual players who actually fund the game are completely ignored. You are simply riding on the legend of the game at this point. This fundamentally broken system is undoubtedly driving many dedicated players to League of Legends, and I am now one of them. I will be canceling my long-term subscription upon making this transition. A system designed to punish toxicity should not relentlessly punish your most dedicated players for trying to win.

title: Request to rework or remove the current Communication/Behavior system in Dota 2
body: ### Description **Request to rework or remove the current Communication/Behavior system in Dota 2** Hello Valve, I would like to ask you to seriously reconsider the current Communication/Behavior system in Dota 2. The problem is that a system designed to reduce toxicity has started to negatively affect one of the most important parts of Dota 2 - communication between teammates. Dota 2 is a team game. Players need to communicate constantly: call missing heroes, suggest objectives, coordinate Roshan, smokes, buybacks, item timings, team fights, lane swaps, defensive actions and dozens of other situations. However, the current system creates an environment where players are increasingly afraid to communicate at all. Players avoid using voice chat, text chat and sometimes even pings because any active interaction with teammates can potentially result in reports and a reduction of Communication Score. As a result, the safest way to protect your account and Behavior Score is simply to remain silent. This creates an absurd situation: **The optimal behavior in a competitive 5v5 team game is to avoid communicating with your team.** The consequences are clearly visible in matchmaking: * players rarely use voice chat; * important information is not communicated; * teammates do not discuss strategy; * players are afraid to criticize even obvious gameplay mistakes; * communication often starts only when the match is already lost; * coordinated play in solo matchmaking becomes significantly harder; * reports can effectively be used as a punishment for disagreement rather than actual toxic behavior. There is also an important distinction between **toxicity** and **communication that another player simply does not like**. Insults, harassment, racism, threats and intentional spam should obviously be punishable. But saying things such as: "Don't fight without buyback." "Please stop farming and come Roshan." "We need BKB before the next fight." "Don't go high ground now." "Can you TP bottom?" should not create a risk for a player's ability to communicate in future matches simply because another player disagreed with the call and decided to report them. The current system incentivizes silence instead of healthy team communication. I believe Valve should either substantially redesign this system or remove the communication restrictions in their current form. Possible improvements could include: 1. Separate actual toxic behavior from ordinary gameplay communication and disagreements. 2. Reduce the influence of mass communication reports when there is no evidence of abusive behavior. 3. Make Communication Score penalties more transparent so players understand exactly what behavior resulted in a restriction. 4. Do not remove essential team communication tools from players unless there is clear evidence of serious or repeated abuse. 5. Introduce stronger protection against report abuse after lost matches. 6. Evaluate the content and context of communication instead of relying primarily on the number of reports. 7. Preserve essential strategic communication such as voice, pings and gameplay calls wherever possible. Dota 2 is one of the most complex competitive team games ever created. Communication should be encouraged, not treated as a potential risk to the player's account. A system intended to combat toxicity should punish toxic behavior. It should not make silence the safest strategy. Please consider reviewing the current Communication/Behavior system and its impact on actual teamwork in matchmaking. Thank you. ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) _No response_ ### Screenshots _No response_

title: Behavior Score system unfairly penalizes solo players in unranked due to party reports and false Overwatch convictions
body: ### Description Hello Valve / Dota 2 Team, I enjoy Dota and play it whenever I have free time. However, for several years now, I have been stuck in what feels like a nightmare of this game, with a Behavior Score fluctuating between 0 and 5,000. Since I don't play Ranked, I don't have the option to avoid parties. As many players know, party players tend to report solo players, shifting the blame for their own poor performance onto the one player who isn't in their group. This happens very often. Currently, I can't even reach 3,000 Behavior Score. It feels like the system intentionally places me in matches right when I'm about to hit that mark, matching me with a full party of four players — which means four reports. This leads me straight into Overwatch. And Overwatch, as it stands, almost always returns a guilty verdict. There are discussions where people admit they click "Guilty" on every case without reviewing the replay at all. As a result, you lose 1,000 points from the verdict, and the reports also throw you into Low Priority games, where you continue to get reported endlessly. In total, you lose around 1,500 points, and you're back to 1,000 Behavior Score. The cycle repeats endlessly, and there is simply no way out of it in the current state of the system. I see many other players reporting similar issues on your GitHub. About two months ago, I finally became so frustrated that I took a break after receiving 4 Low Priority games. I returned recently for the event and noticed that matchmaking had been reworked — I hoped the Behavior Score system had received some attention as well. Unfortunately, that wasn't the case. I struggled through those Low Priority games, managed to play 4 All Pick matches, and then received another punishment from Overwatch. In all 4 of those games, I was the only solo player on my team. There were constant pings directed at me, insults, and likely reports as well. I played well in all of those matches, and there was absolutely no valid reason for a penalty. I realize that nobody is going to review these games, but to support my claim, here is the Match ID from which I received the punishment: 8956143152. By the way, in that same match, the Terrorblade player destroys his items at 48:18. But naturally, no one will report him because he is playing with his friends in a party and can do whatever he wants — they are just having fun. I believe there are several ways to improve this system and potentially bring back hundreds, or even thousands, of players who have left because of these issues. For example: 1. Introduce a "Behavior Score Reset Token" as a reward in one of the events, at least once a year — for instance, in the Quartero's Curios event at level 150. This token would be non-tradable, non-giftable, and usable only once per account, setting the Behavior Score to its maximum value. Ruiners would drop back down in just a few games anyway, so this wouldn't harm normal players in any way. 2. Extend the "Avoid Party" feature to unranked matches, just as it already exists in Ranked. This would at least partially prevent situations where a solo player receives 4 reports and ends up in Overwatch, leading to automatic Low Priority games. 3. Increase the accountability and quality standards for Overwatch reviewers. Currently, there is no penalty for reviewers who hand out "Guilty" verdicts without properly reviewing the evidence. Implementing a quality check or a verification mechanism for Overwatch cases would ensure that only genuine griefers are punished, and innocent players are not caught in a faulty automated loop. I see many posts here about the flaws in the Behavior Score system, and I truly hope you take this feedback into consideration. Thank you for your time and for this incredible game.

title: Feedback/Rework Request: The current Communication Score and In-Game Mute system is fundamentally flawed
body: ### Description The current Communication/Behavior Score system and its automated in-game mutes are actively hurting the matchmaking experience. Dota 2 is a highly competitive, team-oriented game that requires constant communication. The problems with the current mute system are: 1. System Abuse: The automated mute system is easily abused. Players frequently use communication reports to punish teammates for bad gameplay (missed spells, lost lanes), rather than actual toxicity. 2. Collateral Damage: A globally muted player cannot coordinate with their team (calling missing, Roshan timings, smoke ganks). This essentially punishes the 4 other innocent players on the team who are now playing at a severe disadvantage. 3. Impossible to Recover: Once a player's communication score drops, it is incredibly difficult to raise it back up because they cannot communicate to be commended, creating a vicious cycle. Suggested changes to rework the system: - Replace the forced absolute mute with a "soft mute". By default, the player is muted, but teammates should have a clear button to manually UNMUTE them if they want to coordinate. - Do not restrict essential gameplay pings and basic chat wheel commands for muted players. - Rework the automated penalty system so that report volume alone doesn't trigger immediate, severe communication bans without actual text/voice chat analysis. Please reconsider how this system operates, as it currently causes more frustration than it prevents. 4. Encouraging Griefing: The sudden in-game mute often demoralizes the team and triggers griefing behavior. For instance, in a recent match, immediately after a player received a system mute mid-game, two other teammates simply gave up and stopped playing entirely. The match instantly devolved into a chaotic, unplayable state, completely ruining the competitive integrity of the game. ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) 8949763997 ### Screenshots _No response_

title: Bug / Suggestion: /roll command is disabled under low priority / muted chat — causes role disputes in unranked/non-role queue
body: There is a long-standing and very frustrating issue in Dota 2 related to the communication system and the Behavior Score system. When a player has a low behavior score, is in low priority, or is in a muted/punished chat pool (due to reports), the in-game chat becomes restricted or disabled. As a result, the /roll command (which generates a random number to resolve disputes) stops working in all modes, including normal non-role queue matches (All Pick without strict role assignment). What this leads to: Draft Chaos. When two players both want to play mid (or carry/offlane), they have no fair way to decide who gets the role. Double Mid Syndrome. Since /roll is unavailable, players just lock a second mid hero anyway, turning the game into a toxic mess from minute zero. Game Ruining. Instead of a civilized resolution, arguments escalate, players start flaming each other, and often intentionally feed or grief because the dispute is only resolved by "who picks faster". Inequality. This issue disproportionately affects players with low behavior scores — who are already in a bad spot. Instead of giving them tools to resolve conflicts peacefully (like rolling), the system takes that tool away, making matches even more unbearable and preventing them from recovering their score. The Core Problem: /roll is NOT a social chat message; it is a gameplay mechanic (a console/chat command) that returns a random integer. Muting chat or restricting communication should not affect gameplay commands, especially in non-role queue modes where /roll is the only civilized way to distribute roles. Proposed Solution: Make the /roll command available regardless of "Low Priority", "Muted", or "Low Behavior Score" status. Alternatively, add a "Roll" button directly to the hero selection UI that is always functional (similar to how it works in tournament/captain's mode drafts or custom lobbies). This is a critical quality-of-life improvement for the community that would significantly reduce toxicity and the number of ruined games.

title: Behavior Score and Communication Score — concerns about the reporting system!!!
body: Hello Dota 2 developers and community, I would like to ask for clarification regarding the current Behavior Score and Communication Score system. My current scores are: Behavior Score: 12,000 / 12,000 (maximum) Communication Score: 5,800 / 12,000 I regularly play Dota 2 and I do not intentionally grief, feed, destroy my items, abandon matches, throw games, or smurf. In ranked games, I play the roles assigned to me by the matchmaking system and try to play for the win. I also support Dota 2 financially and enjoy the game, which is why I would like to understand how this system works and how it could potentially be improved. I recently checked my Steam Personal Game Data → Dota 2 → Account → Incoming Match Player Report. My recent data shows Communication Reports even during periods where I had no abandons or excessive reports. For example: August 11: - 15 matches - 15 positive matches - 0 reported matches - 0 abandons - 3 Communication Reports from 2 reporting parties August 8: - 15 matches - 14 positive matches - 1 reported match - 0 abandons - 4 Communication Reports from 3 reporting parties August 6: - 15 matches - 11 positive matches - 4 reported matches - 0 abandons - 7 total reports - 4 Communication Reports from 4 reporting parties August 2: - 15 matches - 15 positive matches - 0 reported matches - 0 abandons - 0 Communication Reports My main question is: How can a player have a maximum Behavior Score of 12,000/12,000 while having a Communication Score of only 5,800/12,000? I understand that these are separate systems and that Communication Reports can affect Communication Score. However, I am concerned about the possibility of unjustified or retaliatory reports. There is another situation that I believe is worth considering. In a five-player team, it is possible that three players are in the same party and know each other. If one of these players has a disagreement with me, the other two party members may potentially report me simply to support their friend, even if they did not personally witness any actual communication violation. In this situation, what could start as a disagreement between two players could potentially result in multiple reports against the same player simply because several players are grouped together. For example, instead of receiving one report from the player involved in the disagreement, I could potentially receive reports from all three members of the party because they want to support their friend. This raises an important question: Does the Communication Score system take party relationships or coordinated/retaliatory reporting into account? If multiple members of the same party report the same player, are these reports treated completely independently, or does the system recognize that they may be related to the same incident? I believe this is important because otherwise a single conflict between two players could potentially have a disproportionately large effect on another player's Communication Score. Players can report each other because of disagreements, frustration after losing a game, disagreements about gameplay decisions, or personal conflicts. Therefore, I would like to understand how the system prevents abuse of Communication Reports. I contacted Steam Support about this issue. They told me that the scores are automated and that Steam Support cannot manually adjust them. They also stated that they do not provide additional information about how the behavior scoring system is calculated. They recommended that I bring this issue to the Dota 2 community and development forums. So this is what I am doing. I am NOT asking for my Communication Score to be manually increased. I would simply like to understand whether the current system can incorrectly penalize a player because of unjustified, retaliatory, or potentially coordinated Communication Reports, and whether there are mechanisms that prevent players from abusing the reporting system. I would also like to raise another question regarding the recovery of Communication Score. Why does the Communication Score not have some form of regular recalibration or review period, for example once a year? Would it be possible to introduce an annual recalibration, review, or another mechanism that would give players who have demonstrated consistently good behavior over a long period of time a clearer way to recover their Communication Score? In my subjective opinion, there appears to be a significant imbalance between losing Communication Score and recovering it. It feels like a player can receive Communication Reports relatively easily and potentially lose Communication Score very quickly, while recovering that lost score through consistently good behavior appears to be much slower. Even if a player makes a serious effort to communicate politely and avoid violations over a long period of time, recovering from a low Communication Score can feel extremely difficult. In other words, the negative effect of reports can appear very quickly, while the positive effect of consistently good behavior takes much longer to become visible. I believe that a regular recalibration or another transparent recovery mechanism could make the system feel more fair. It would also give players a clearer motivation to improve their behavior because they would know that consistently good behavior over time can meaningfully restore their Communication Score. If there is no way for players to verify whether reports against them were legitimate, how can they know what behavior they need to change? I would appreciate any clarification from the Dota 2 developers or experienced players who understand how the current system works. I am not asking for special treatment for my account. I am asking whether the current system could be improved to make Communication Score more resistant to report abuse and to provide players with a reasonable path to recover from a low score through consistently good behavior. I have attached screenshots of my Personal Game Data as evidence. Thank you for taking the time to read this and consider the issue.

title: Behavior Score
body: ### Description Title: Feedback / Suggestion: Behavior Score system needs real-time updating and better balance for isolated bad games Body: Hi Valve team, I’d like to share some feedback regarding the current Behavior & Communication Score system. Currently, receiving a summary every 15 games makes the system feel rigid and unfair. A player can play 14 great games, have 1 bad game (or get targeted by a toxic party/tilted teammates), and end up with a heavily penalized report or even low priority. One single bad match shouldn't outweigh two weeks of good behavior. Suggestions for improvement: Real-time updates (similar to modern mobile competitive games): Instead of waiting 15 games for a batch update, let every single match influence the score dynamically. Weighted Recency: Recent games should hold meaningful weight, but isolated incidents shouldn't drastically ruin an entire reporting period. Better Variance Protection: A single bad game out of 15 should be treated as an anomaly, not a trend. This change would make the system feel much more transparent, fair, and encouraging for players who are actively trying to maintain high behavior scores. Thanks for your time and hard work! ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) _No response_ ### Screenshots _No response_

title: [Suggestion] Improved Communication Score system: Immediate All-Chat mutes and heavy deductions to stop toxicity without driving players away
body: ### Description ### Summary The current report and communication score system in Dota 2 feels too passive. Bad actors can severely insult opponents in All-Chat, ruin everyone's emotional state, and they only receive a minor score deduction matches later. We need a firmer, faster, and more transparent approach to protect the player base from toxicity. ### Why we need this (Balancing Environment and Player Retention) We understand that Valve needs to maintain its player base. Permanently banning or suspending accounts for chat toxicity can be counterproductive, as it drives players away entirely and ruins matchmaking times. Instead of banning the account, we should strictly "strip away their ability to ruin the game environment" while still letting them play the game. Keeping them in the game but forcing them into silence is the perfect balance for player retention and community health. ### Proposed Solutions 1. **Immediate All-Chat Time-out (Real-time Mitigation):** If the system detects severe toxic keywords or verified report spikes in All-Chat, that player should be instantly and automatically muted from All-Chat for the rest of the match or the next 24 hours. Stop the toxicity in its tracks before it spreads to other players. 2. **100% Automated System Reading (No Human Check Needed):** The system should automatically scan all chat logs using a pre-defined blocklist of toxic words, slurs, and toxic gaming jargon (e.g., "ez", "noob", "trash", "dog", etc.). There is no need for manual human checkers. If the text matches the filter, the penalty is executed immediately by the server. 3. **The "First-Striker" Principle (Protecting Those Who Reply):** Often, a toxic player starts the insults, and their teammates or opponents only reply out of frustration. The system should only punish the **first person** who initiates the toxic behavior in that specific chat timeline. Anyone who replies or defends themselves afterwards should NOT be penalized. Punishing the "first striker" stops the root cause of the toxicity without unfairly striking back at victims who are just reacting to provocation. 4. **Heavier Penalties for Severe Insults (-2000 Score):** Ruinous behavior shouldn't cost just 100 points. Severe toxic words should trigger a massive, immediate deduction (e.g., -2000 communication score). Since players lose All-Chat privileges when dropping below 10,000 points, one single toxic outburst should instantly silence them for dozens of matches until they earn it back. 5. **Transparency (Show the Evidence Log):** When players lose score, the client should show them a notification displaying exactly which log/words triggered the penalty. They need to know precisely *what* they typed that led to the punishment. Winning a game shouldn't be an excuse to demean opponents. Respecting the enemy team is basic sportsmanship, and Valve can enforce it strictly through precise, heavy chat restrictions without having to ban players from playing. ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) _No response_ ### Screenshots _No response_

title: Proposal: Replacing the current Behavior Score system with a transparent, disciplinary model
body: ### Description ​The current Behavior Score system is detrimental to the Dota 2 experience. It fails to distinguish between unavoidable technical issues (power/internet outages, hardware failures) and intentional disruptive behavior. As a result, players are trapped in a "point of no return," where recovery is nearly impossible. ​The game is fundamentally a team-based experience, yet this system forces players into a state of "silent survival." Players are now terrified to use voice or text chat to coordinate, as any interaction can trigger retaliatory reports from teammates. This silence destroys the core of Dota 2, as communication is essential for team play. ​Furthermore, this system drives players to abandon their main accounts and create new ones, which devalues the competitive integrity of the game. ​Proposed Reforms: ​Remove the Hidden Behavior Score: Replace the current hidden point system with a transparent and predictable disciplinary model. ​Clear Penalties for Abandoning: Instead of a complex score reduction, implement direct consequences for technical issues. For example: 3 abandons = 5 games of Low Priority. ​Targeted Communication Bans: If a player receives reports from all 9 other players in a single match, they should receive a 48-hour communication ban. If the behavior persists, the punishment should escalate to Low Priority matches without access to chat for the purpose of "correction." ​Low Priority Revamp: Replace the mandatory "Single Draft" (SD) mode in Low Priority with "All Random" (AR). This makes the punishment less monotonous and keeps the game engaging, even for those serving time. ​Address Report Abuse and the Overwatch System: The current report system is heavily abused as a weapon against teammates. Furthermore, the "Overwatch" system is ineffective because reviewers often lack context or are biased, leading to unfair judgments. We need a system that filters out malicious, weaponized reports rather than penalizing any form of communication. ​The goal should be to encourage positive communication and team play, not to force players into "mute mode" or drive them away from the game entirely. I urge the development team to reconsider the current model in favor of a more transparent and fair disciplinary framework. title: Suggestion: Improve Behavior Score Recovery
body: This is not a bug report. I'd like to suggest a possible improvement to the current Behavior Score and Communication Score system. I wanted to share some feedback about the current Behavior Score and Communication Score system in Dota 2. The system has been in the game for almost three years now, and I think it has one major problem: once a player drops to a very low Behavior Score, it's extremely difficult to recover. You can play many games without abandoning or griefing and still gain only a small amount of Behavior Score. At the same time, it's very easy to lose hundreds of points from reports. Sometimes it feels like simply using chat is enough to get reported, even if you're just trying to communicate with your team. Because of this, many players can't use voice and text chat altogether. Others create new accounts just so they can play normally again, communicate with teammates, and queue for Ranked. I don't think that's the goal of the system. I think it would be worth considering some kind of amnesty or reset after all this time. Here are a few possible ideas: * Restore every account that isn't permanently banned to 12,000 Behavior Score and Communication Score. * If a full reset is too much, raise everyone below a certain threshold (for example, 8,000) to a healthier level. * Make Behavior Score recover much faster for players below 8,000, so they have a realistic chance to climb back. * Reduce Behavior Score losses from reports unless those reports are confirmed by the system. * Consider a one-time recovery event for long-term active players who haven't abandoned games or received confirmed griefing penalties for a long period. The system has already been in place for nearly three years. By now, players who wanted to improve their behavior have had plenty of time to do so. A one-time reset would give those players a fair chance to start over, while players who continue to be toxic would naturally lose their score again. The reason I'm suggesting this is simple. Right now, players with low Behavior Score often feel stuck. They can spend weeks trying to improve it and make almost no progress, while losing hundreds of points again after just a few matches. It becomes frustrating enough that many people simply stop playing on their main account. I also believe this would reduce the number of new accounts being created. Right now, many players feel that creating a new account is much easier than trying to recover their main account, and that's probably not the outcome the system was designed to encourage. I believe giving players another chance after almost three years would improve communication, reduce the number of new accounts being created, and make the system feel much fairer. Players who continue to be toxic would naturally lose their Behavior Score again, so the purpose of the system would remain the same. I really enjoy Dota 2, and I'm only writing this because I think this change would make the game better for a lot of players. Thank you for your time. I'd also like to hear what other players think. Have you had a similar experience with recovering Behavior Score?

title: Player Behavior Summary Punishes Poor Performance Instead of Actual Misconduct
body: ### Description # **The Current Player Behavior System Creates Silent Matches and Makes Recovery Nearly Impossible** I have been playing Dota 2 for many years, and I believe the current Player Behavior Summary system has serious flaws that are damaging the quality of matches and the social experience of the game. For nearly a year, my Behavior Score has remained around 3000. During this time, I have had very limited communication privileges, rarely communicate with other players, do not abandon matches, and do not intentionally grief games. Despite this, my score barely changes and meaningful recovery appears almost impossible. The main issue is that the system does not seem to adequately distinguish between intentional griefing and simply having a bad game. When a team loses, frustrated players often report their teammates. A player can make mistakes, have a poor performance, or simply be unlucky without intentionally ruining the match. However, those reports still contribute to a punishment system that can trap players at low Behavior Scores for extremely long periods of time. Another consequence is that many matches have become completely silent. Players are afraid to communicate because they fear reports and further penalties. Others have already lost access to communication features. As a result, matches often contain: * No leadership * No strategic discussion * No coordination * No planning * No meaningful social interaction Dota 2 is fundamentally a team game. Communication is one of its most important elements. A system designed to improve player behavior should not create an environment where players are afraid to speak. My questions to the Dota team are: 1. How does the system distinguish between intentional griefing and simply performing poorly? 2. How is a player expected to recover from a very low Behavior Score if reports continue to outweigh positive behavior? 3. Is the current system achieving its intended goal, or is it simply creating silent matches where players avoid communication altogether? I understand the need to punish toxic behavior, intentional griefing, and abusive communication. However, the current system appears excessively punitive and offers very little transparency regarding how players can realistically recover. I hope the Dota team will review the long-term effects of this system and consider whether it is truly improving the player experience or unintentionally harming it. # The Current Player Behavior System Creates Silent Matches and Makes Recovery Nearly Impossible I have been playing Dota 2 for many years, and I believe the current Player Behavior Summary system has serious flaws that are damaging the quality of matches and the social experience of the game. title: Smoke of Deceit activation message is attributed to the player as a personal chat message, enabling false "communication abuse" reports
body: ### Description When a player activates Smoke of Deceit, the in-game notification that appears in team chat ("[Player] used Smoke of Deceit" / smoke activation message) is being treated by the report system as a personal text-chat message sent by that player. Because of this, other players can report me for communication abuse (text chat / voice toxicity) based solely on the automated smoke notification — even though I have no access to text chat or voice communication at all. My communication is restricted (Communication Score: 5200), and I have never sent a chat message or used voice in these games. This is critical: in Dota, a communication report can only be submitted for voice toxicity or text-chat toxicity. Game-ruining behavior is tracked under a separate, general "Reports" metric (see column 10 in the attached statistics). The reports I am receiving are landing under the communication category (column 12) — which is logically impossible, because I have no communication access for which I could be reported. Timeline proving the bug The correlation is exact: toxicity reports against me started immediately after the Smoke update was released, even though I have never had chat access during that period. My text chat was only unlocked for a single short window: from 2026-06-05 13:46:59 GMT to 2026-06-08 17:43:51 GMT. Outside of that window, my Behavior Score was below 6,000, so chat/communication was locked entirely. Despite chat being locked, the communication reports kept coming in — coinciding precisely with matches in which I activated Smoke of Deceit. This confirms the smoke notification is being misattributed as my own communication. title: A transparent, fair mechanic to restore Behavior Score via Single Draft
body: I’d like to propose a clear, transparent mechanic for restoring Behavior Score one that is easy for every player to understand, beneficial for the entire community, and designed with anti-abuse safeguards in mind. The problem Losing Behavior Score is correctly designed to be quick, while regaining it is slow. However, the exact way to recover is currently unclear to most players. There are no visible, fixed parameters that guarantee progress, which leads to frustration and a sense of helplessness especially among those who ended up in low-priority or low-Behavior Score pools by accident. The proposal Make Single Draft games a predictable source of Behavior Score restoration. Specifically: +10 Behavior Score for any completed Single Draft match, regardless of outcome. +50 Behavior Score for a Single Draft win. This applies only to Single Draft games not already accounted for by the current system. Why these numbers Given that an average match already yields a small variable amount of Behavior Score through commend-based or time-based recovery, these fixed bonuses are small enough not to devalue positive conduct in other modes, yet meaningful enough to provide a visible, reliable path forward. The 5:1 ratio between a win and a loss maintains a healthy incentive to play seriously, while still acknowledging effort even in defeat. Why Single Draft It naturally pushes players out of their comfort zone, broadening hero pools and improving adaptability — this raises the general skill level of the player base. It acts as a fair recovery environment for players who were placed in low priority due to circumstances beyond their control (internet or power outages, emergency situations, etc.), without excusing genuinely disruptive behavior. Anti-abuse considerations To prevent exploitation (e.g., intentionally losing to farm Behavior Score), the bonus could be capped at a limited number of Single Draft games per day or per week. Additionally, the bonus should not apply to matches where the player is flagged for AFK, griefing, or excessive reports preserving the integrity of the system.
