title: GitHub Acceptable Use violations led to Dota2-Gameplay turning into unusable mess.
body: For years, this repository was one of the most useful public places for Dota 2 players to report gameplay issues, document bugs, and communicate problems in a way that could realistically be seen by Valve developers. It served as a direct and practical channel between the player community and the people maintaining the game. Unfortunately, over the last few months, that value has been seriously damaged by the constant activity pattern of a specific user: @Dota-Explorer. I am naming the account only so Valve and/or GitHub staff can review the issue history, blocking behavior, duplicates, reposting patterns, and overall impact on the repository. This report is not about targeting a person for having opinions or for reporting bugs frequently. The concern is about repeated disruptive behavior that is making the issue tracker significantly less useful for everyone. I myself, as well as other notable community members, such as @Leamare or @sikleq, were harassed and blindly accused by this user multiple times - both on- and off- GitHub. ## Reference to GitHub Acceptable Use Policies I believe this situation should be reviewed in the context of GitHub’s Acceptable Use Policies: In particular, GitHub states that collaboration only works when users are able to work together in good faith. The policies also mention that GitHub does not allow activity that is off-topic or interacts with platform features in a way that significantly or repeatedly disrupts the experience of other users. This report is not intended to claim that a violation has already been definitively proven. Rather, I am asking Valve and community contributors to review whether the repeated issue flooding, reposting of closed topics, and blocking of community discussion may fall under disruptive use of GitHub Issues, spam-like behavior, or misuse of platform features. ## Main Concern The problem is not simply that this user posts a lot. High activity by itself is not necessarily harmful if the reports are accurate, useful, and open to normal discussion. The issue is that the repository is being flooded with an excessive number of issues every single day, many of which appear to be duplicates, misleading, unverifiable, based on personal accusations, or not actual gameplay bugs. This volume of posts makes it much harder for legitimate reports to be noticed. Important bugs and useful technical issues are quickly pushed down or buried under a constant stream of low-quality issues. For example, real WebAPI issues have already been reported and then quickly piled up under unrelated or lower-quality reports. In-game Economics bugs also become much harder to notice, even though those can have real impact on players, items, rewards, purchases, and the overall game experience. This is especially damaging because Dota 2 has many different categories of issues that require attention: gameplay bugs, server problems, WebAPI issues, item/economy bugs, UI problems, matchmaking issues, cosmetics, replays, tooltips, and more. When one user dominates the issue tracker with constant posts, the whole reporting system becomes harder to use. Important issues from other users become less visible, harder to search for, and less likely to receive discussion or confirmation. ## Reposting and Artificial Visibility What makes the situation worse is the repeated pattern of closing topics and then reopening or recreating them when they do not receive attention. This creates artificial visibility and keeps the same topics circulating again and again, even when there is no meaningful new information. This turns the issue tracker from a structured bug-reporting system into something closer to a personal complaint board. It also makes it harder for developers and users to distinguish between a genuinely urgent issue and a reposted or duplicated claim. ## Blocking Other Users from Discussion Another serious problem is the use of GitHub’s blocking system. This user appears to be blocking a large number of other community members, which prevents those people from replying to, correcting, or discussing the issues being posted. As a result, the user can publish biased, incorrect, duplicated, or accusatory information while limiting the ability of others to challenge or clarify it. This is unfair to other users and harmful to Valve developers who may rely on issue discussions to understand whether a report is valid. An issue tracker should allow the community to help verify information. If a report contains false claims, missing context, duplicate information, or an incorrect interpretation of game behavior, other users should be able to point that out. When one person can block many of the users who disagree with them and still continue posting large numbers of issues, the process becomes one-sided and unreliable. It creates the appearance of community consensus where none exists, while preventing normal discussion from happening. ## Unofficial Triage and Self-Appointed Confirmation Another concern is that @Dota-Explorer appears to be creating an unofficial parallel triage system inside the repository. They frequently add `#ConfirmedByDEXP` to bugs reported by other users and then include those reports in their own repeatedly created threads. This gives the impression that reports have been formally reviewed, confirmed, or organized through some recognized process, even though this appears to be only the user’s personal label. This is misleading and disruptive. It can make ordinary user comments look like official confirmation, while also redirecting attention from the original reports into @Dota-Explorer’s own threads. In practice, this turns other users’ bug reports into material for a personal tracking system rather than allowing the repository’s normal issue process to work. The issue is not that a user is trying to help confirm bugs. Community confirmation can be useful when done in good faith and without misleading presentation. The problem is the repeated use of a personal confirmation tag, combined with excessive issue creation, reposting, and blocked discussion. Together, this creates a parallel, self-appointed triage process that competes with the actual issue tracker and makes the repository harder to navigate. This also adds to the flooding problem. Instead of keeping discussion focused in the original reports, issues are repeatedly pulled into separate threads, making it harder for Valve developers and other users to follow the original context, reproduction details, and corrections. ## Impact on Developers and Real Bug Reports This behavior has also made the repository much less productive for developers. Instead of receiving clear, focused, reproducible bug reports, users now have to sort through constant noise, repeated claims, personal accusations, and discussions that are intentionally limited by blocking. This wastes time and reduces the chance that real gameplay, WebAPI, and in-game economy issues will be found, confirmed, and fixed. The impact is not theoretical. When serious technical topics such as WebAPI issues or in-game Economics bugs get buried, the entire community loses. ## Why This Is Damaging The current situation is damaging for several reasons: 1. Legitimate bug reports are being buried by excessive issue spam. 2. Important reports, including WebAPI and in-game economy issues, become harder to notice. 3. Duplicate and low-quality reports make the issue tracker harder to search and maintain. 4. Other users are prevented from correcting false or misleading information. 5. Developers receive a distorted view of community feedback. 6. The repository is becoming hostile, unproductive, and increasingly unusable. 7. The issue tracker is being used less like a public bug-reporting tool and more like a personal complaint board. 8. Reopened or recreated issues keep pushing the same topics back to the top without adding useful new information. 9. Unsupported accusations and unverifiable claims create unnecessary conflict and confusion. 10. The normal community process of confirming, reproducing, or disproving bugs is being undermined. ## Clarification I understand that users should be allowed to report bugs frequently, and I do not want to discourage legitimate reports and I completely support the desire to make our favorite game a better place. However, the current pattern appears to go beyond normal participation. The concern is not @Dota-Explorer criticizing the game. The concern is the repeated creation of large numbers of low-quality or duplicate issues, combined with blocking other users who try to correct or discuss them. This should not be allowed to continue. A single user should not be able to dominate the repository, block opposing voices, repeatedly repost closed topics, and present biased or incorrect claims without meaningful community input. ## Possible Solutions ### 1. Add restrictions on how many issues a single user can create per day, week, or month This would probably be the most practical solution. It would not target one specific person unfairly, and it would reduce spam without completely preventing users from reporting bugs. A reasonable limit would force users to prioritize the most important reports instead of opening dozens of issues in a short period of time. It would also help ensure that reports from other users remain visible. This seems especially important because banning one account may not solve the problem. If the user can simply create a new account and continue the same pattern, then broader issue creation limits would be more effective than only account-specific punishment. ### 2. Apply constant moderation to the issue tracker This would help if every low-quality, duplicate, unsupported, or accusatory report could be reviewed and closed quickly. However, this is obviously unrealistic. Developers and maintainers should not have to spend large amounts of time manually cleaning up the issue tracker every day just because one user is flooding it. Moderation can help, but it is not a realistic long-term solution by itself. ### 3. Close down the public Issues section completely This would stop the spam problem, but it would also be very unfortunate for the wider community. The repository has historically been one of the best ways to report real Dota 2 issues directly. Closing Issues entirely would punish everyone because of the behavior of one or a few users. It would also make it harder for legitimate bugs to be reported and tracked publicly. This should probably be considered only as a last resort. ### 4. Ban or limit the specific user This may be necessary if the behavior continues, but a simple ban may not solve the problem completely. The user could simply create a new account and continue the same behavior. Because of that, account-specific action should probably be combined with broader rate limits or moderation rules. Limiting the user’s ability to create new issues may be more effective than only banning the account. ## Recommended Approach Out of these options, the best approach would likely be some combination of issue creation limits and targeted bans for frequent violations. A general rate limit would reduce spam without relying on constant manual cleanup, while specific action could still be taken against accounts that repeatedly abuse the system. This would be more fair to the wider community than closing Issues entirely, and more effective than simply banning one account. ## Closing This repository used to be one of the best resources for reporting and tracking real Dota 2 gameplay problems. Right now, it is becoming increasingly unusable because of one user’s repeated disruptive activity pattern. Important reports are being flooded, technical issues are becoming harder to notice, and normal community discussion is being blocked. This appears inconsistent with the spirit of GitHub’s Acceptable Use Policies, especially the expectation that users should be able to collaborate in good faith without repeated disruption. For the sake of player-to-developers communication, health of the game and the wider player community, this needs to be addressed in a fair, transparent, and constructive way. Thanks in advance for noticing this issue. I sincerely wish this place to be a safe one and, most importantly, a healthy one going long-term.

title: Overwatch system overhaul
body: Dear Dota Team, I am writing to express my growing frustration with the current reporting and Overwatch system in Dota. After approximately 7,000 hours of gameplay, I have experienced and supported the game extensively. It is therefore all the more disappointing for me to see that the current system, in my opinion, is not working fairly. Players are seemingly reported regardless of their actual behavior or their Behavior Score. Reports appear arbitrary and have noticeable negative consequences, even when no wrongdoing has occurred. For example, if you back a buy, even if you overlook the fact that your TP is on cooldown, you get reported, immediately receive a 24-hour Overwatch ban, five SD games, and a 1,000-point score penalty. This development significantly impacts the enjoyment of the game. In its current form, I find the game barely playable, as the system does not adequately differentiate between actual misconduct and unfounded reports. I therefore urge you to fundamentally revise the reporting and Overwatch system. A more transparent, fairer, and more reliable system is urgently needed to sustainably improve the player experience. I've also attended all the TI events. This doesn't just affect me, but many other players as well. Please revise your system so that, for example, three Overwatch reports result in a penalty. This would ensure that toxic players are detected anyway, preventing such misjudgments. Many players blame the replay because they were frustrated by the last match. If this situation doesn't change, I will be forced to reconsider my investments in the game and sell my in-game items. Furthermore, I will refrain from making any further purchases in the future. I sincerely hope you take this feedback seriously and consider taking appropriate action.

title: Concerns Regarding Behavior Score System, Matchmaking Quality, and Ranked Structure in Dota 2
body: I would like to raise a serious concern regarding the current gameplay experience in Dota 2, specifically related to the behavior score system and matchmaking quality. Almost every time I queue for a match, the games feel extremely unbalanced. On one side, there are account buyers who clearly do not belong in their bracket, and on the other side, there are obvious smurf players using highly complex heroes with unnatural ease and dominance. This creates a very frustrating environment that feels unfair and discouraging. Under these conditions, it becomes increasingly difficult to stay calm and composed. Even when I communicate normally through voice chat, my behavior score continues to drop. It feels like the system is punishing players for reacting to problems that are not being properly addressed in the first place. Additionally, reporting smurfs appears to have little to no impact. Many of these cases are extremely obvious, yet no visible action is taken. This gives the impression that reports are ineffective and discourages players from using the system at all. Another issue is that the lower the behavior score gets, the worse the matchmaking quality becomes. This creates a negative loop where players are pushed into increasingly toxic and unbalanced games, making it even harder to improve their behavior score. A potential solution would be to introduce seasonal rank resets. If ranks were not permanent, boosting services would lose their value, as purchased MMR would not last. This could significantly reduce smurfing and account buying, and help restore fairness to the matchmaking system. At that point, it would be reasonable to evaluate player behavior more strictly, as the gameplay environment itself would be more balanced and fair. Right now, however, it feels like the system focuses more on silencing players rather than addressing the root causes of frustration. I hope you take this feedback seriously and consider improving both matchmaking integrity and the effectiveness of the reporting system.

title: Unfair report / behavior system impacting Communication Score for party players
body: Hello Valve Support / Dota 2 Team, I’m writing to report a recurring problem with Dota 2’s reporting and Conduct Summary system that is negatively affecting my account’s Communication and Behavior scores. Problem summary I primarily play as a duo with a friend. In about half of our games we are matched with a group of three (trio) on the other team. Frequently those opposing trios grief and then report my friend and me together, even when we have not done anything to deserve a report. Because multiple players from the same party submit reports, our accounts receive multiple reports in a single match (often three reports each), which appears to disproportionately affect our Communication and Behavior scores. As a result, our communication score has dropped significantly and we’re finding it extremely difficult to recover it despite playing consistently and not engaging in the behaviors cited. This feels unfair because coordinated reporting by parties of friends can be used to punish other players without valid cause. Why this is a problem It encourages misuse of the reporting system by coordinated groups. It penalizes players who are not at fault and makes it hard to restore reputation. The current system does not appear to account for context (matched parties, retaliation, or false reporting by the same party across matches). Suggested fixes / requests Consider implementing weighting or de-duplication of reports from the same party in a single match (e.g., treat reports from multiple players in the same party as a single report for scoring purposes). Add better transparency in Conduct summaries about why specific penalties or score drops occurred, including when multiple reports from the same party were a factor. Provide a clearer, faster appeals path or manual review for players who believe they were falsely or unfairly reported due to coordinated griefing/retaliation. Improve heuristics to detect coordinated false-reporting patterns across matches and discount or flag them. Supporting details My Steam ID / account: ibra_malallah / 76561198291661601 Please let me know if you need more information. I appreciate any attention you can give to this issue—this system is hurting legitimate players and reducing the quality of matchmaking. Thank you, Ibrahim Malallah
author: ibmalallah98-afk

title: Behavior score system is easily abused and punishes innocent players
body: ### Description I lost around 1000+ behavior score recently despite playing normally. Facts: - No abandons - No intentional feeding - Played every match until the end - Chat muted (so no toxic communication) What actually happened: - Teammates griefing (AFK, leaving lane early, not playing properly) - Those same players reported me out of frustration - System punished me based on reports quantity, not actual behavior This creates a broken situation: - Players can spam reports without consequences - No real validation of gameplay - Innocent players lose behavior score for nothing Current system problems: - Quantity-based punishment instead of quality-based review - No protection against false reports - No detection of real griefing (AFK, inactivity, lane abandoning) Result: The system punishes players who try to play properly, while actual griefers often stay unpunished. Suggestions: - Add validation for reports (not only number-based) - Detect AFK / inactive players more strictly - Reduce impact of reports when player has consistent normal gameplay Right now, it feels unfair and discouraging to play. ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) _No response_ ### Screenshots _No response_

title: Ranked matchmaking bans
body: Don't know if thats the place to post such problem, but steam support directed me here without resolving my issue. So my problem is with my account being matchmaking banned basicly 2-3 times a month for 24h. My account atm is 6000 mmr my communication score is 12000 and behavior is 6100.Tho i think com score is maxed out at the behavior score level. Problem started after few abbandons that happened on pick phase (accepted match and didnt pick in time). After that my behavior score dropped to around 8000 and i was placed in smurf pool, from that point however hard i tried to climb it back it always at some point got hit by 24h ban and -1000 score.So i'am stuck here for 3 months already with no clue what to do. 90% of games i play now look the same: People pick hard support juggernauts or phantom assassins and after 5 mins game is basicly over cause they lost lane and go to jungle without fullfiling their roles.I thought i'll play supports every game to maybe solve this issue by myself.But then i see the same guy picking juggernaut offlane and it ends in the same way.(Yes avoid system doesnt work?) Even if the picks are decent the people i'am getting have accounts with like 500 hours played.I assume these are bots accounts bought on 3rd party sites.Which ends up in the same way since a guy who bought account faces people that are playing way better, so the outcome is basicly set. There are some games that people actually play and try their best to enjoy the game.But even in these games either in my team or opponents have a guy that literally go AFK.Turned off my chat like 2 months ago cause of toxicity in these games and the fact that despite having english choosen i basicly see english words in like 1 out of 30 games. I have some bad games myself:For example yesterday before i got another 24h ban i played Venomancer pos 1 and after me and my bounty hunter sup killed opponents i think 5/6 times on this lane.I was left allone and ganked by the whole enemy team without my team not even reacting.We eventually won the game but i was forced into such a defensive stance ( since they had legion commander ) that i barelly could connect to my team.After the game ended i got banned again.Never in this or my previous games i was trying to ruin someones else experience, like going afk, destroying items or stealing someones farm and not playing my role. So yeah this situation for me looks pathetic, i have some friends who are divine immortals but majority are like legend ancients so i cant even stack as 5 man to grind that behavior up. So i end up with people that report me despite me not acting in a way to be reported. What wonders me tho is that i'am constantly checking my reports score and ammount of reports i recieve on the personal game data page on steam.And most of the time i have 0 reportes and my behaviour goes up, and that comes a game that i get an insta 24ban right after and like 4 days ago i checked that page and still had 0 reports from that match despite getting 24h ban and -1000 behaviour.

title: Persistent "No Steam Log on" Errors
body: ### Description This report concerns recurring "No Steam Logon" errors affecting account 1473342547. Over the past three days, multiple matches have been interrupted by forced disconnects followed by this specific error message, despite a stable local network connection. As similar incidents have been reported by numerous other users recently, the evidence suggests a systemic technical fault in the Steam authentication or game server infrastructure rather than an isolated client-side issue. The automated penalty system has incorrectly flagged these technical disconnects as intentional abandons. Consequently, account 1473342547 has been subjected to matchmaking bans, Low Priority placement, and a significant reduction in behavior score. These penalties are a direct result of the aforementioned infrastructure instability and do not accurately reflect player conduct. I request a technical investigation into these logon failures and the restoration of my account status. Specifically, I am asking for the removal of the matchmaking cooldown and Low Priority requirements, and for the behavior score to be restored to its state prior to these incidents. The relevant data for these matches can be verified through the logs associated with ID 1473342547. ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) 8747440327 ### Screenshots _No response_

title: #MAKEDOTAGREATAGAIN
body: We, representatives of the CIS Dota 2 community, as well as, in essence, a significant portion of the global Dota 2 player base, would like to formally express our deep concern regarding the current state of the game and its direction in recent years. Dota 2 has long been more than just a game for us - it is a competitive environment, a community, and a cultural phenomenon. However, many long-standing issues continue to negatively impact the player experience, and we believe they are not receiving the attention they deserve. 1. Behavior Score System The current behavior score system is widely perceived as ineffective and, in many cases, unnecessary. Instead of improving match quality, it often creates frustration and imbalance. The system discourages communication between players, lacks fairness, and at times does not accurately reflect actual in-game behavior. As a result, it reduces overall enjoyment of the game. 2. Ranked System The ranking system raises serious concerns. The gap between skill levels and MMR brackets is extremely large, making progression disproportionately difficult and time-consuming. For many players, ranking up requires an unrealistic investment of time, which reduces long-term engagement and motivation. 3. Cheating and Fair Play One of the most critical issues is the growing presence of cheaters in public matches. This problem severely undermines competitive integrity. Many players believe that anti-cheat measures are insufficient and that enforcement actions are nearly nonexistent. A stronger and more transparent stance on fair play is urgently needed. 4. Quality of Updates Recent updates are perceived as lacking depth, coherence, and clear direction. Changes often feel unfinished or disconnected from the needs of the community. This creates the impression that development is no longer guided by a clear vision for the game. 5. Gameplay and Balance There is growing concern regarding the current gameplay direction and overall balance of the game. The meta is heavily dominated by aura-based items, which reduces strategic diversity and limits viable playstyles. Matches have shifted away from dynamic teamfights toward prolonged farming, making gameplay feel slower and less engaging. Additionally, the current comeback mechanics often lead to excessively long games, even in situations where one team has a clear advantage. Overall, there is a strong ощущение that player feedback is not being adequately considered, and that balance decisions are disconnected from the community’s expectations. 6. Lack of Meaningful Events Over the past year, there has been a noticeable absence of engaging and memorable in-game events. Historically, events have played a key role in maintaining player interest and community enthusiasm. Their decline has led to a significant drop in overall engagement. 7. Technical Issues, Bugs, and Server Stability There is growing concern regarding the overall technical condition of the game. Players frequently encounter bugs that remain unresolved for extended periods of time. In addition, server instability has become a recurring issue - matches can suffer from severe lag, sometimes lasting 30 minutes or more, directly impacting game outcomes and ruining the competitive experience. Furthermore, numerous visual and interface-related bugs reduce usability, negatively affecting play. Taken together, these issues create the impression of insufficient attention to the technical quality of the game. We are writing this not out of negativity, but out of genuine concern for the future of Dota 2. We believe in the game’s potential and its legacy, and we hope to see it thrive once again. We strongly urge greater transparency, closer communication with the community, and decisive action on the issues outlined above. Respectfully, The CIS Dota 2 Community

title: #MakeDotaGreatAgain
body: We, representatives of the CIS Dota 2 community — as well as, in many ways, a considerable part of the global Dota 2 player base — would like to formally express our serious concerns about the current state of the game and the direction it has taken in recent years. For us, Dota 2 has always been more than just a game. It is a competitive space, a community, and a cultural phenomenon. However, a number of long-standing issues continue to negatively affect the player experience, and it feels as though they are not receiving the level of attention they require. Behavior Score System The current behavior score system is widely viewed as ineffective and, in many situations, unnecessary. Rather than improving the quality of matches, it often leads to frustration and imbalance. The system discourages player communication, lacks transparency and fairness, and sometimes fails to accurately reflect actual in-game behavior. As a result, it diminishes the overall enjoyment of playing. Ranked System The ranking system is another source of concern. The gap between skill levels and MMR brackets has become extremely large, making progression disproportionately difficult and time-consuming. For many players, climbing the ranks requires an unrealistic amount of time investment, which ultimately decreases long-term motivation and engagement with the game. Cheating and Fair Play One of the most pressing problems is the increasing presence of cheaters in public matches. This issue seriously undermines competitive integrity. Many players feel that the current anti-cheat measures are insufficient and that enforcement actions are rare or ineffective. A stronger and more transparent approach to maintaining fair play is urgently needed. Quality of Updates Recent updates often appear to lack depth, consistency, and a clear sense of direction. Many changes feel unfinished or disconnected from what the community actually needs. This creates the impression that the development process is no longer guided by a clear long-term vision for the game. Gameplay and Balance There is growing concern about the current direction of gameplay and overall balance. The meta is heavily dominated by aura-based items, which reduces strategic variety and limits viable playstyles. Matches have gradually shifted away from dynamic teamfights toward extended farming phases, making the gameplay feel slower and less engaging. In addition, the current comeback mechanics frequently result in excessively long games, even when one team holds a clear advantage. Overall, there is a strong feeling that player feedback is not being sufficiently considered, and that balance decisions are often disconnected from community expectations. Lack of Meaningful Events Over the past year, there has been a noticeable lack of engaging and memorable in-game events. Historically, such events played an important role in keeping the community excited and involved. Their absence has contributed to a decline in overall player engagement. title: #MakeDotaGreatAgain
body: #MakeDotaGreatAgain We, representatives of the CIS Dota 2 community, as well as, in essence, a significant portion of the global Dota 2 player base, would like to formally express our deep concern regarding the current state of the game and its direction in recent years. Dota 2 has long been more than just a game for us - it is a competitive environment, a community, and a cultural phenomenon. However, many long-standing issues continue to negatively impact the player experience, and we believe they are not receiving the attention they deserve. 1. Behavior Score System The current behavior score system is widely perceived as ineffective and, in many cases, unnecessary. Instead of improving match quality, it often creates frustration and imbalance. The system discourages communication between players, lacks fairness, and at times does not accurately reflect actual in-game behavior. As a result, it reduces overall enjoyment of the game. 2. Ranked System The ranking system raises serious concerns. The gap between skill levels and MMR brackets is extremely large, making progression disproportionately difficult and time-consuming. For many players, ranking up requires an unrealistic investment of time, which reduces long-term engagement and motivation. 3. Cheating and Fair Play One of the most critical issues is the growing presence of cheaters in public matches. This problem severely undermines competitive integrity. Many players believe that anti-cheat measures are insufficient and that enforcement actions are nearly nonexistent. A stronger and more transparent stance on fair play is urgently needed. 4. Quality of Updates Recent updates are perceived as lacking depth, coherence, and clear direction. Changes often feel unfinished or disconnected from the needs of the community. This creates the impression that development is no longer guided by a clear vision for the game. 5. Gameplay and Balance There is growing concern regarding the current gameplay direction and overall balance of the game. The meta is heavily dominated by aura-based items, which reduces strategic diversity and limits viable playstyles. Matches have shifted away from dynamic teamfights toward prolonged farming, making gameplay feel slower and less engaging. Additionally, the current comeback mechanics often lead to excessively long games, even in situations where one team has a clear advantage. Overall, there is a strong ощущение that player feedback is not being adequately considered, and that balance decisions are disconnected from the community’s expectations. 6. Lack of Meaningful Events Over the past year, there has been a noticeable absence of engaging and memorable in-game events. Historically, events have played a key role in maintaining player interest and community enthusiasm. Their decline has led to a significant drop in overall engagement. 7. Technical Issues, Bugs, and Server Stability There is growing concern regarding the overall technical condition of the game. Players frequently encounter bugs that remain unresolved for extended periods of time. In addition, server instability has become a recurring issue - matches can suffer from severe lag, sometimes lasting 30 minutes or more, directly impacting game outcomes and ruining the competitive experience. Furthermore, numerous visual and interface-related bugs reduce usability, negatively affecting play. Taken together, these issues create the impression of insufficient attention to the technical quality of the game. We are writing this not out of negativity, but out of genuine concern for the future of Dota 2. We believe in the game’s potential and its legacy, and we hope to see it thrive once again. We strongly urge greater transparency, closer communication with the community, and decisive action on the issues outlined above. Respectfully, The CIS Dota 2 Community

In addition, server instability has become a recurring issue - matches can suffer from severe lag, sometimes lasting 30 minutes or more, directly impacting game outcomes and ruining the competitive experience. Furthermore, numerous visual and interface-related bugs reduce usability, negatively affecting play. Taken together, these issues create the impression of insufficient attention to the technical quality of the game. We are writing this not out of negativity, but out of genuine concern for the future of Dota 2. We believe in the game’s potential and its legacy, and we hope to see it thrive once again. We strongly urge greater transparency, closer communication with the community, and decisive action on the issues outlined above. Respectfully, The CIS Dota 2 Community ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) _No response_ ### Screenshots _No response_

title: #MakeDotaGreatAgain
body: ### Description We, representatives of the CIS Dota 2 community, as well as, in essence, a significant portion of the global Dota 2 player base, would like to formally express our deep concern regarding the current state of the game and its direction in recent years. Dota 2 has long been more than just a game for us - it is a competitive environment, a community, and a cultural phenomenon. However, many long-standing issues continue to negatively impact the player experience, and we believe they are not receiving the attention they deserve. 1. Behavior Score System The current behavior score system is widely perceived as ineffective and, in many cases, unnecessary. Instead of improving match quality, it often creates frustration and imbalance. The system discourages communication between players, lacks fairness, and at times does not accurately reflect actual in-game behavior. As a result, it reduces overall enjoyment of the game. 2. Ranked System The ranking system raises serious concerns. The gap between skill levels and MMR brackets is extremely large, making progression disproportionately difficult and time-consuming. For many players, ranking up requires an unrealistic investment of time, which reduces long-term engagement and motivation. 3. Cheating and Fair Play One of the most critical issues is the growing presence of cheaters in public matches. This problem severely undermines competitive integrity. Many players believe that anti-cheat measures are insufficient and that enforcement actions are nearly nonexistent. A stronger and more transparent stance on fair play is urgently needed. 4. Quality of Updates Recent updates are perceived as lacking depth, coherence, and clear direction. Changes often feel unfinished or disconnected from the needs of the community. This creates the impression that development is no longer guided by a clear vision for the game. 5. Gameplay and Balance There is growing concern regarding the current gameplay direction and overall balance of the game. The meta is heavily dominated by aura-based items, which reduces strategic diversity and limits viable playstyles. Matches have shifted away from dynamic teamfights toward prolonged farming, making gameplay feel slower and less engaging. Additionally, the current comeback mechanics often lead to excessively long games, even in situations where one team has a clear advantage. Overall, there is a strong ощущение that player feedback is not being adequately considered, and that balance decisions are disconnected from the community’s expectations. 6. Lack of Meaningful Events Over the past year, there has been a noticeable absence of engaging and memorable in-game events. Historically, events have played a key role in maintaining player interest and community enthusiasm. Their decline has led to a significant drop in overall engagement. 7. Technical Issues, Bugs, and Server Stability There is growing concern regarding the overall technical condition of the game. Players frequently encounter bugs that remain unresolved for extended periods of time. In addition, server instability has become a recurring issue - matches can suffer from severe lag, sometimes lasting 30 minutes or more, directly impacting game outcomes and ruining the competitive experience. Furthermore, numerous visual and interface-related bugs reduce usability, negatively affecting play. Taken together, these issues create the impression of insufficient attention to the technical quality of the game. We are writing this not out of negativity, but out of genuine concern for the future of Dota 2. We believe in the game’s potential and its legacy, and we hope to see it thrive once again. We strongly urge greater transparency, closer communication with the community, and decisive action on the issues outlined above. title: Suspected MVP System Bias, Inconsistent Awards, and Potential Gameplay Probability Issues in Dota 2
body: ### Description Dear Steam Support and the Dota 2 Development Team, I am writing to formally report serious concerns regarding what appears to be a broken, inconsistent, and potentially biased MVP award system in Dota 2. I am also requesting an investigation into suspicious patterns involving critical hits, Bash procs, and other probability-based gameplay mechanics. I have been experiencing these issues repeatedly across multiple matches, and the frequency of these occurrences has become extremely frustrating. In many games, the MVP awards do not appear to reflect the actual contributions and performance of the players involved. Some results make very little sense when compared with what happened during the match. I believe the MVP system requires a thorough review to determine whether its scoring criteria, calculations, or implementation are functioning as intended. I have personally lost approximately 50 MVP awards that I believe I should have received based on my performance. I understand that MVP selection may involve multiple factors, but the repeated inconsistencies warrant a closer examination. I am also concerned about the behavior of probability-based mechanics, including critical hits, Bash effects, and similar random or chance-based outcomes. I would like the development team to investigate whether these mechanics are operating according to their intended probabilities and whether match data reveals any unusual patterns. I am not claiming to have definitive proof of deliberate manipulation, but the recurring nature of these incidents has raised serious concerns for me. I would appreciate an evidence-based investigation rather than having these reports dismissed without examining the relevant match data. My concerns are particularly serious because I have also observed discussions and apparent irregularities involving professional matches. If similar issues are occurring at that level, it would be important to establish whether there is a legitimate technical explanation and whether any changes are necessary to protect competitive integrity. I experience what I consider inconsistent or unfair MVP outcomes almost daily, across multiple games. I have attached evidence from my most recent match for your review. I request that the team examine this match alongside the relevant performance statistics, MVP scoring criteria, combat logs, and probability-based event data wherever available. I respectfully request the following actions: Conduct a thorough review of the MVP award system and its scoring criteria. Investigate whether MVP awards are being calculated consistently and fairly across comparable match performances. Review the attached match evidence and explain the reasoning behind the MVP decision, where possible. Examine whether critical hits, Bash procs, and other probability-based mechanics are behaving within their intended parameters. Investigate recurring reports of similar issues, including any verifiable irregularities in professional matches. Confirm whether these systems are functioning as designed and whether corrective action or a future update is necessary. Dota 2 is a competitive game in which players invest considerable time and effort into improving their performance. Players deserve confidence that the systems evaluating their contributions and determining gameplay outcomes are functioning correctly. I am requesting a serious technical investigation, a meaningful response, and appropriate corrective action if any problems are identified. I would also appreciate clarification on how MVP awards are calculated and what evidence players can provide to help verify suspected inconsistencies. Thank you for your time. I look forward to a response addressing these concerns and the attached match evidence. Sincerely, A Concerned Dota 2 Player ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) _No response_ ### Screenshots _No response_

title: Request for a new ban wave against matchmaking data exploits / pre-match overwolf-like apps
body: Hello Dota 2 Team / Gabe, I am writing to ask for another ban wave against third-party applications that exploit player data during the pre-game draft phase (like Overwolf overlay apps and similar software). Even though Valve previously introduced privacy updates to hide player profiles before the picking phase ends, some third-party tools still find workarounds to read match logs or memory data. This allows users to target-ban opponent signature heroes, which ruins the competitive integrity of Ranked Matchmaking. Please protect honest players and conduct another massive wave of bans against those who use unauthorized software to gain an unfair meta-advantage during drafts. Thank you.

title: Request for manual review of an old permanent matchmaking restriction
body: ### Description Hello Dota 2 team, I am creating this issue because I have been unable to get a manual review of an old matchmaking restriction through Steam Support. My Dota 2 account has been permanently restricted from matchmaking since approximately 2019. My last Dota 2 match was played in 2019, meaning that this restriction is now approximately seven years old. I have contacted Steam Support multiple times regarding this restriction. Each time, I received the same standard response stating that the Dota team determined that the account had engaged in one or more forms of negative behavior and that Steam Support would not lift the restriction. I understand the reason that has been provided to me. I am not asking for confidential information about Valve's detection systems, and I am not asking Steam Support to repeat the same explanation again. My request is for an actual manual review of this old restriction. I have specifically asked Steam Support to escalate my case to a senior representative or the Dota team, but my requests have been answered with the same standard response and the ticket has been closed. The original restriction message indicated negative behavior such as: - A consistent pattern of user reports, negative conduct, and player abuse - Feeding - Abandoning - Non-participation in matches At the time, I also had an unstable internet connection, which could cause disconnects and low-priority penalties. I acknowledge that I may have made mistakes in the past, and I am not trying to deny the possibility of negative behavior from that period. However, approximately seven years have now passed. I have not played Dota 2 since 2019. My internet connection and hardware are stable now, and I would like to return to Dota 2. I am not asking Valve to ignore its rules or disclose internal enforcement information. I am asking whether the Dota team can manually review an approximately seven-year-old permanent restriction and reconsider whether I can be given one opportunity to return to matchmaking. I can provide screenshots of my previous Steam Support conversations showing the repeated standard responses and my requests for escalation. Thank you for taking the time to read this and consider my request. ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) _No response_ ### Screenshots

title: Appeal for Investigation into Permanent Dota 2 Account Ban
body: ### Description Hello Valve Team, I am writing once again to respectfully ask for a manual review of the permanent ban on my Dota 2 account and to request clarification regarding the reason for this decision. Over the past several months, I have made every reasonable effort to contact you. I have submitted Steam Support tickets, created GitHub issues, sent emails, and even attempted to reach out through every official channel I could find. Unfortunately, I have never received a response explaining why my account was permanently banned or whether my case has ever been manually reviewed. I have been a Steam and Dota 2 player for over 16 years and have always tried to follow every rule described in the Steam Online Conduct and the Steam Subscriber Agreement. I have never knowingly violated any rule or intentionally participated in any activity that could justify a permanent ban. If I have unknowingly done something that violated your policies, I sincerely ask you to tell me what it was. Without any explanation, I have no way to understand what happened, learn from it, or even determine whether this ban was applied correctly. Throughout my years of playing Dota 2, I have invested thousands of hours into the game. My account reflects my commitment as a player, for example, I have played nearly 7,500 matches while abandoning only 29 of them. I believe this demonstrates that I have always taken the game seriously and respected both my teammates and the community. I fully understand that Valve does not disclose every detail of its anti-cheat and anti-abuse systems, and I am not asking you to reveal sensitive detection methods. I am only asking for a fair manual review of my account and confirmation that the permanent ban was applied correctly. If a mistake has been made, I respectfully ask that it be corrected. If the ban is indeed justified, I would greatly appreciate receiving at least a general explanation of the category of violation that led to it. Remaining permanently banned without any understanding of the reason has been extremely frustrating, especially after being a loyal player for so many years. This is not an attempt to argue with your policies or waste your time. I am simply asking for fairness, transparency, and the opportunity to understand what happened to my account. Thank you for taking the time to read my message. I sincerely hope someone from the Dota 2 team will review my case and provide a response. Kind regards, centralnui ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) _No response_ ### Screenshots _No response_

title: For years the conduct system now has been completely worthelss, unfair and frankly. Not working as intended.
body: ### Description For years the conduct system now has been completely worthless, unfair and frankly. Not working as intended. Not only does it take months to climb back conduct - 1 overwatch report will send you back months. (on average most people gain 150-300 conduct score. (IF they manage to play without getting any reports) 1 report will give you minus 500-1000. For the average player, that would take months to regain, assuming you only get an update after 15 games, and most players play 2-3 games weekly. Not only that, the unfair treatment, Why do you even get game reported for game behavior if you have have most kills assist golds cs hero damage?, in counter-strike you can do whatever the fuck you want, where as in dota valve treat the game completely different?. Also lower ranked players like archons and crusaders should not be allowed to overwatch much higher ranked MMR games? people at that level has 0 business conducting reports of player behaviour outside their bracket. What may seem like griefing for them, is part of the game in higher brackets. It's time to remove the endless reports from people, the community throw reports left and right in each game once the someone doesn't play the game they want you to play it. Give limited reports that are earned only by true successful, so that people actually think about reporting enemies and teammates and not just toss them mindlessly every game. Not only that, even if you play MUTED without inbound chat, you're able to report teammates for communication, another alarming signal that the conduct system is flawed and needs a big overhaul. ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) _No response_ ### Screenshots _No response_

title: Dota 2 Ban Dispute – Request for Evidence and Clarification
body: Hello, I am writing again to request a manual review of the long-term ban on my Dota 2 account, as I have not received any response to my previous ticket submitted about a month ago. I fully understand that support teams can be busy, but the complete lack of communication regarding this issue is extremely frustrating, especially considering the length of the ban and the absence of any explanation. I have been a loyal Steam and Dota 2 player for over 16 years and recently received my 16-year Steam loyalty badge. Throughout this time, I have always made a conscious effort to follow all rules, play fairly, and respect the community. I have never knowingly used cheats, exploits, third-party software, or engaged in any behavior that would justify a permanent ban. I have always followed everything stated in the Steam Online Conduct and the Steam Subscriber Agreement, and I am not aware of having violated any of these rules. My account has now been banned for over 461 days, yet I still have not received any clear explanation, warning, or evidence regarding the reason for this action. This leaves me in a situation where I cannot understand what happened or how to prevent it in the future. To summarize: - I have always played legitimately - I have no history of cheating or abusive behavior - I have not received prior warnings or serious penalties - I have invested many years into Dota 2 Additionally, while I cannot currently access Dotabuff due to the ban, I ask you to review my available statistics. I have played 7,487 matches and abandoned only 29, which I believe reflects my consistent and fair approach to the game. I respectfully ask for one of the following: - A manual review of my account and the applied ban - A clear explanation of the reason for the ban - Any evidence or details that led to this decision If there has been a mistake, I kindly request that it be corrected. If not, I ask for transparency so I can at least understand the situation. I have already attached relevant information in my previous ticket, including a screenshot of my last matches before the ban. I genuinely care about my account and the many years I have dedicated to the game. All I am asking for is a fair review and clear communication. Please take a moment to investigate my case. Thank you for your time. Sincerely, centralnui

title: Appeal from a Dedicated Dota 2 Player of 12+ Years
body: Hello, I am writing to request a manual review and clarification regarding a long-term ban on my Dota 2 account, which I believe may have been applied in error. I have been a loyal Steam and Dota 2 player for over 16 years and recently received my 16-year Steam loyalty badge. Throughout all these years, I have always tried to follow the rules, play fairly, and respect the community. I have never intentionally used cheats, exploits, third-party software, or engaged in any behavior that would justify a ban. I have always respected everything written in the Steam Online Conduct and the Steam Subscriber Agreement, and I have never knowingly broken any rules. Despite this, my account has now been banned for over 418 days, and I still have not received any clear explanation about the reason for the ban. I did not receive prior warnings, notifications, or evidence of wrongdoing. This situation is very frustrating and confusing for me because: - I have always played legitimately. - I have no history of cheating or toxic behavior. - I have never received serious penalties before. Dota 2 has been one of my main games for many years. At the moment I cannot open Dotabuff while my account is banned, but I kindly ask you to look at the available statistics. I have played 7,487 matches and abandoned only 29. In my opinion, this record clearly reflects my attitude toward the game and my commitment to playing fairly and responsibly. The lack of information makes it impossible for me to understand what might have triggered this penalty or how to avoid similar issues in the future. If there was a mistake, I would greatly appreciate it being corrected. If there is a specific reason, I respectfully ask for clarification. If it helps, I have attached a screenshot showing my last games before I was permanently banned. I care deeply about my account and the time and effort I’ve invested into the game over the years. I simply want a fair review and an opportunity to continue playing. Please investigate my case and consider manually reviewing the ban. Thank you very much for your time and assistance. Sincerely, centralnui

title: Communication report system is broken & unfair
body: Hello, I’m submitting a formal complaint regarding my Communication Score, because the current situation is unfair and does not make sense. Right now my Communication Score is below 6000, and I cannot use text chat or voice chat at all (both are disabled). However, my Communication Score still continues to decrease. My question is straightforward: how can my Communication Score go down if I literally cannot type or speak? If communication is disabled, I cannot be “toxic” through chat/voice — so this looks like an automated punishment system that keeps applying penalties without real, verified behavior. What’s happening in practice is that when a team loses, people often mass-report players on the losing team out of frustration. I’m being punished by reports that do not reflect actual misconduct, and this creates a loop where I can never recover, because: I cannot communicate at all, I still get reported simply for losing matches, and my score keeps dropping with no meaningful way to improve. This is not a fair behavior system — it traps players permanently even when they are trying to play normally. I request a manual review of my account and a clear explanation of: What is causing the score to drop while chat is disabled; Whether these reports are considered communication-related or gameplay-related (and why they affect “communication”); What a realistic recovery path is, if reports can be abused like this; Ideally, a re-evaluation/reset based on my recent match history. If this cannot be reviewed or corrected, I will simply stop playing, and I will consider uninstalling Steam/Dota 2, because the experience has become frustrating and pointless under a system that keeps punishing me without allowing me to communicate. Info (if needed): Last visible update: 05/02/2026 Conduct Score: 11,903 Communication Score: 5,834 I can provide Match IDs / screenshots if required I appreciate a serious review and response. Thank you.

title: Behavior system is broken and needs a rework.
body: ### Description This system needs a rework for the reasons i've listed below: **1. Commends have no weight** It appears that no matter how many commends you get after a match, 5, 10, 15, etc. - they do not increase your behavior score, yet a single report could decrease it by 150 points. Reports have a lot more weight than commends even though it's just as easy to report someone as it is to commend them. This inequality makes it easier to lose your behavior score and stunts your progress to regain it. **2. Inability to stop an abandon/AFK** Having a behavior score of less than 5k makes you more susceptible to losing because you have no way to prevent a player from going afk as a result of disconnecting. As a result the team with a disconnected player has a serious disadvantage over the team that has no players that disconnected. Keep in mind that can also apply to you if you disconnect, because you get thrown in a pool of players that have the same or lower behavior score than you. **3.Unnecessary mutes** You can mute a toxic player in the scoreboard if you want, both their voice chat and text chat by clicking a few buttons. There is no need for a permanent mute if the mute feature is already present in the match. If anything permanently muting a pool of players only hurts teamplay by making them unable to make game-saving calls. **4. Vicious cycle.** Unstoppable abandons and disconnects and reports having literally infinitely more weight than commends create a system where once you get below a threshold of 5k the chances of you ever climbing out of that bottomless pit are near-zero. **5. Smurfing** But hey, there is a solution to all these problems, just create a new account, where you can start over, and create even more disbalance in the matchmaking. **Conclusion** This behavior system creates and encourages even more unfair matches, smurfs and boosters. My solutions are removing the communication score and a 5k pausing threshold from the game. Valve, please. Fix this system and prevent dota 2 from becoming a 2nd post-meet your match Team Fortress 2. **EDIT** Some people reached out to me to link their steam discussion here (why tf does it have 1.2k replies), if there's any russian speakers you might as well read the initial post in the discussion because It's **WAY** more informative than mine. title: [Performance] Severe FPS Drops on High-End CPU (i7-14700K): Main Thread Stalls due to Lock Contention in tier0.dll
body: ### TL;DR I conducted a deep profiling of heavy FPS drops in teamfights on a high-end rig (**i7-14700K + RTX 4080 Super**). **The verdict:** The issue is NOT E-Cores or Thermal Throttling. The issue is severe **Thread Lock Contention** in `tier0.dll`. The engine is wasting **>50% of CPU cycles** just waiting for memory locks instead of rendering frames. --- ### The Setup Like many players, I get massive FPS drops during heavy teamfights (MK Ult, PL illusions, etc.) despite having top-tier hardware. * **CPU:** i7-14700K (P-Cores pinned, running at 5.5GHz stable) * **GPU:** RTX 4080 Super * **RAM:** 64 GB DDR5-6000 * **OS:** Windows 11 (Optimized) ### The Investigation I got tired of guessing, so I hooked **Intel VTune Profiler 2025** to the game process to see exactly what happens at the code level when the FPS tanks. ### The "Smoking Gun" Findings The trace data reveals a **disaster in thread management** during particle-heavy scenes. #### 1. It's NOT the Scheduler First, I debunked the myth that the game gets thrown onto E-Cores. VTune confirms the Main Thread stays on P-Cores. The hardware is doing its job perfectly. #### 2. Tier0.dll is the Bottleneck (Lock Contention) The function `CAtomicMutex::AcquireLock` in `tier0.dll` becomes a top hotspot with a **horrific CPI (Cycles Per Instruction) rate of ~10.5**. > **Translation:** The CPU is spending 10x more effort *trying to get permission* to calculate something than actually calculating it. Threads are fighting each other for access, causing the game to stutter regardless of CPU speed. #### 3. The "Dead" CPU Time The Main Thread shows **53.7% Back-End Bound**. This means for more than half the time during a teamfight, my i7-14700K is **doing nothing**. It's just stalling, waiting for data from memory because the engine's particle system (`particles.dll`) creates a massive bottleneck in the L2/L3 cache and RAM. ### Visual Proof I have attached the screenshots from Intel VTune showing the timeline and hotspots. ### Conclusion We cannot fix this with hardware upgrades. This is a fundamental scalability issue in the engine's threading model (likely legacy code in `tier0.dll`). **The engine is effectively choking itself.** ### To the Devs I have attached the exported CSV analysis below. I can provide the full `.etl` trace file / VTune project folder upon request. [result_function.csv]( [result_pcores.csv](

title: Why no one is questioning the current Behavior Score system. Will Valve make any adjustments to it?
body: Before I begin this post, let me clarify that I always play in anonymous mode and rarely type in chat. Before this year, my Behavior Score had always been maintained at the perfect 12,000 points. However, this year, after experiencing two or three crashes due to an input method bug, my Behavior Score plummeted to just over 9,000 points. At that time, it was still somewhat acceptable. But then something I absolutely cannot tolerate happened: when a solo player like me gets reported by a premade stack in Turbo Mode, their Behavior Score gets directly deducted. And each time, it drops by 500 to 1,000 points. What’s worse, there’s a widely spread rumor in the community that reporting others can increase your own Behavior Score. This has led to players with low Behavior Scores frantically reporting each other. As long as you get reported by the majority of players, your Behavior Score plummets even further. And so, my Behavior Score dropped from 12,000 at the beginning of the year to just 6,500 points now. Since my score fell below 8,500, I haven’t typed a single word in-game. Let me give a few examples of the most unacceptable Behavior Score deductions I’ve experienced: I encountered a three-stack where all three players went to the same lane. As a position 1 carry, I was completely abandoned and had no choice but to jungle. Yet, that three-stack reported me, and my Behavior Score was directly deducted by about 500 points. In a Turbo Mode game, I first-picked Faceless Void as position 1 and marked my lane. However, my teammate last-picked Juggernaut, competing for my role. I gave up the position 1 role and voluntarily went to jungle. By the end of the game, I had dealt 40% of the total team damage. Still, after the match, my Behavior Score was deducted by 500 points. These are just two simple examples, but they are the ones I find most unbearable. Not to mention being reported by more players in lower brackets who don’t understand the game or the situation. Now, with my Behavior Score at 6,500 points, after a 10-game winning streak, I encountered 30 consecutive matches where, when I picked support, my teammates picked four support heroes, and when I picked a core role, my teammates had economy stats like a traffic light by the 6-minute mark. This Behavior Score system feels like hell. I’m just an ordinary player—why can’t I enjoy the game? I also want to experience the joy of gaming, to fight alongside my teammates. I always commend teammates who get a "Rampage," but when I get a "Rampage," I’ve never received a single commend from my teammates. I’ve even encountered a Nature's Prophet who bought back and used his ultimate just to last-hit and steal my "Rampage." If Valve ever sees this post, I hope you will make adjustments to the Behavior Score system. Let every player enjoy the game fairly and return to us the joyful gaming environment we deserve.

title: Communication score dropping even without reports or chat activity (false penalty case)

I have **not used voice or text chat** in the last week, and have received **dozens of commendations** instead. This seems to indicate that the communication score system is triggering penalties even when no communication is made. ### 🧠 Expected Behavior If a player does not communicate (or communicates positively) and receives no reports, the communication score should remain stable or increase — not decrease. ### 💬 Suggestion Valve should review the detection rules for “communication activity” and consider: - Ignoring “muted by peers” if no text/voice was sent. - Avoiding penalties for inactivity in chat. - Decoupling player grouping effects (low-score teammates) from communication score. - *This issue affects legitimate players who play silently or with minimal communication and still get punished unfairly. ### 🎯 Additional Context: Support Players Are Disproportionately Affected As a support player, I’ve noticed that the matchmaking system frequently pairs me with teammates (cores) that have very low performance or low behavior scores, despite my own account being at the maximum 12,000 behavior rating. This issue seems systemic: - Supports often have **no direct control over farming or game outcome**, yet are heavily affected by the quality of cores assigned to them. - The matchmaking algorithm appears to **prioritize balancing MMR globally** without considering role impact, resulting in **unfairly skewed lobbies** for high-behavior supports. - In practice, this leads to **consistent pairing with underperforming cores**, and therefore, **no MMR progress despite strong individual play and conduct**. This might explain why **high-behavior support players** experience: - Stagnation or decline in rank. - Frustration despite playing clean, communicative matches. - A perception that the system "punishes" supports who queue solo. title: Group Reports in Turbo Ruins my Behavior score
body: ### Description Report system in Turbo JUST ACCEPTS Party reports as valid by default Of course. After analyzing the provided data from your Dota 2 Personal Game Data, here is a clear breakdown of why your Behavior Score (BS) is falling, focusing on the issue of reports from parties. ### Executive Summary Your analysis is correct. The data strongly suggests that you are a positive player who receives a healthy number of commends. However, your Behavior Score is being systematically lowered by a small but consistent number of reports, almost certainly from players in groups who coordinate their reports against you, even when you have done nothing wrong to deserve them. ### Detailed Analysis Here is the evidence from your match history that supports this conclusion: **1. You Are a Generally Positive Player:** * **High Commends:** You consistently receive between 16 and 33 commends per 15-game summary. This is an excellent sign and indicates that many players enjoy having you on their team. * **No Conduct Flags:** You are consistently marked **"No"** for **Excessive Reports** and **Excessive Abandons**. This is a crucial point—it means the system does not consider you a chronically toxic player. * **High Positive Match Rate:** The vast majority of your matches are "Positive Matches" (often 14 or 15 out of 15). **2. The Root Cause: Coordinated Reports from Groups** The key to understanding your dropping BS lies in the `Reports` and `Reporting Parties` columns. * **The Pattern:** Look at the summaries where your BS drops: * `2025-10-30`: 1 Report from 1 Reporting Party. * `2025-10-25`: 1 Report from 1 Reporting Party. * `2025-10-21`: 3 Reports from 3 Reporting Parties. * `2025-10-19`: 3 Reports from 2 Reporting Parties. * `2025-10-17`: 2 Reports from 2 Reporting Parties. * **Why This is Significant:** The "Reporting Parties" number indicates how many *different groups or individuals* reported you. When you see `2 Reports` from `2 Reporting Parties`, it means two separate entities reported you. In Dota, a "party" can be a single player or a group of players queuing together. **The most damaging scenario is when you get reported by a 2, 3, or 4-stack party.** If you have a disagreement with a group, or if they simply need someone to blame for a loss, all members of that party can report you simultaneously. This counts as multiple reports but from a single "Reporting Party." The system weighs this heavily. **3. How This Drives Your BS Down:** The Dota 2 behavior system is automated. It doesn't judge the *validity* of a report in real-time; it sees a correlation: * **The Formula:** A high number of reports relative to your number of games = lower Behavior Score. * **The Injustice:** Even a single report from a 4-stack party in one game can be enough to trigger a "Reported Match" and cause a drop in your BS for that summary period, even if you were completely silent and played your best. Your data shows you often have 1-2 "Reported Matches" per summary, which is enough to cancel out the positive effects of your many commends. **4. The Role of Communication Reports:** While less frequent, you also occasionally receive Communication Reports (`Comms Reports`). The same logic applies. A single negative interaction with a party can lead to multiple `Comms Reports` from one `Comms Reporting Party`, unfairly penalizing you. ### Conclusion You are caught in a systemic problem. You are not a toxic player, as evidenced by your high commend count and lack of excessive reports or abandons. However, you are vulnerable to **coordinated reporting from groups.** When a party of players decides to report you, they can artificially inflate your "reports per match" ratio. The automated system interprets this data as a sign of poor behavior and lowers your score accordingly. Your consistent commends prove you are a good teammate, but they are not enough to fully counteract the punitive weight of these coordinated, and likely unjustified, reports. This creates a frustrating cycle where your BS slowly decays not because of your actions, but because of the social dynamics of a team-based game where groups can easily weaponize the report system against a solo player. ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) ### Screenshots

title: Проблемы с механизмом подачи жалоб в Dota 2 и частые необоснованные блокировки аккаунта
body: ### Description Уважаемые представители Valve Corporation! Обращаюсь к вам по крайне актуальной для меня проблеме, связанной с игрой Dota 2. Моя игровая активность неоднократно сталкивалась с блокировкой аккаунта из-за ложных и необъективных жалоб со стороны других игроков. Эти обвинения абсолютно беспочвенны и существенно влияют на удовольствие от игры. Сейчас система Dota 2 предусматривает пять типов жалоб: Токсичность в чате Токсичность голосом Смурфинг Препятствование игре Читерство Однако многие типы этих жалоб имеют серьёзные недостатки: Жалоба на токсичность голосом: Этот пункт становится бессмысленным, ведь игроки с уровнем порядочности менее 6000 вообще лишаются права голосового общения. Таким образом, жаловаться на голосовую токсичность бессмысленно, поскольку обвиняемый попросту не имеет технической возможности говорить. Жалоба на токсичность в чате: Аналогично предыдущему пункту, уровень порядочности влияет и на использование текста. Игрок с низким показателем порядочности физически не способен отправлять сообщения в общий чат, значит, подать жалобу на токсичность текстом также нелогично. Препятствование игре: Жалобы по этому типу действительно бывают справедливыми, особенно если речь идёт о ситуациях вроде кражи вещей, умышленного отправки союзников в стазис или установки вардов прямо на местах спауна крипов. Однако подобные претензии часто используются неоправданно и становятся причиной незаслуженного наказания. Смурфинг: Эта проблема практически непроверяема без глубокого анализа IP адресов или MAC-адресов компьютеров. Часто игровые сессии проходят в компьютерных клубах, где определить принадлежность устройства затруднительно. Даже дружеские визиты гостей и совместные сеансы на одном компьютере ведут к путанице. Читерство: Обвинения в использовании сторонних программ требуют тщательной проверки. Вы сами располагаете инструментами мониторинга активности, позволяющими выявлять нарушения, тогда как обычные игроки не обладают такими возможностями. Но несмотря на наличие инструментов контроля, множество недобросовестных лиц продолжает распространять чит-программы, что создаёт трудности для честных геймеров. Отдельно хочу отметить ограничение свободы выражения мнений, которое наблюдается в самой популярной онлайн-игре. По всему миру активно действует принцип свободы слова, но именно в Dota 2 взаимодействие между пользователями ограничено настолько сильно, что даже малейшие попытки выразить недовольство расцениваются как нарушение порядка. Очень важно, чтобы средства коммуникации были настроены таким образом, чтобы избегать ситуаций взаимных нападок и недопонимания. Поэтому настоятельно рекомендую пересмотреть работу механизма подачи жалоб и добавить объективные критерии оценки поведения игроков. Предлагаю усилить контроль над теми, кто злоупотребляет системой жалоб, возможно, введя штрафы за ложные утверждения и развивая методы предотвращения распространения нелегальных чит-программ. Подводя итог, хотелось бы надеяться, что компания Valve обратит внимание на указанную проблему и предпримет необходимые шаги для улучшения качества обслуживания игроков и комфорта геймплея. С уважением, Дмитрий Игровой регион: Россия Dear representatives of Valve Corporation, I am writing to you regarding a very important issue that I have encountered while playing Dota 2. My gaming activity has repeatedly faced account bans due to false and unjustified complaints from other players. These accusations are completely unfounded and significantly affect my enjoyment of the game. Currently, the Dota 2 system provides five types of reports: Chat toxicity Voice toxicity Smurfing Obstruction in-game Cheating However, many of these report categories have serious flaws: Voice Toxicity Report: This point becomes meaningless because players with less than 6000 behavior score cannot use voice chat at all. Therefore, it is illogical to file a complaint for vocal toxicity when the accused does not even have technical access to speak. Chat Toxicity Report: Similarly, text communication restrictions apply based on the player's behavior score. Players who do not meet this threshold physically cannot send messages into public chats, meaning filing such complaints also makes no sense. Obstruction in Gameplay: Complaints under this category can be justified if someone steals items or deliberately sends allies into stasis, places wards directly where creeps spawn, or intentionally dies. However, these claims are often used unfairly and lead to unwarranted punishments. Smurfing: This problem is almost impossible to verify without deep analysis of IP addresses or computer MAC-addresses. Many sessions take place in internet cafes where identifying device ownership is difficult. Even friendly visits by guests and shared play sessions on one account create confusion. Cheating: Accusations related to cheating require thorough investigation. While you possess monitoring tools capable of detecting violations, regular players lack such capabilities. Despite having control measures, numerous dishonest individuals continue distributing cheat programs, creating difficulties for honest gamers. It’s worth noting separately how freedom of expression is restricted within what should otherwise be an open platform for interaction between users. In most parts of the world, free speech principles are actively upheld, but Dota 2 imposes severe limitations that make even minor expressions of dissatisfaction count as behavioral violations. It would be crucial to adjust communication methods so they avoid situations leading to mutual attacks and misunderstandings. Therefore, I strongly recommend revising the current reporting mechanism and introducing objective criteria for evaluating player conduct. Consider implementing penalties for those abusing the reporting system, possibly through fines for false allegations, and enhancing measures against illegal cheat software distribution. In conclusion, I hope that Valve will pay attention to this critical issue and take necessary steps to improve service quality and enhance user comfort during gameplay. Sincerely,Dmitry Game region: Russia ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) _No response_ ### Screenshots _No response_

body: Hello, I’ve been playing Dota 2 for many years, mostly in Turbo mode (around 99% of my matches).
