title: Request for Review: False Reports Triggered by Chat Wheel Sounds
body: Hello Valve Team, Recently, I bought a new chat wheel sound effect from Vasilisa with a “kisi-kisi mjau-mjau” sound effect. Sadly, I am being reported because of this sound effect, and as a result, my conduct summary is being reduced. I believe this is a major issue faced by thousands of Dota 2 players all over the world. Since this is an ALL CHAT message, it means that both teams, including enemies, can hear it. Most of the time, people simply submit a random report against the player who owns this chat wheel sound, or any other chat wheel sound, or even for a harmless message such as “Good game, well played.” As a conclusion we got following main issues 1. Players are being unfairly reported for using officially purchased chat wheel sounds. 2. Conduct summary scores are being reduced due to reports unrelated to actual toxic behavior. 3. All-chat messages (including chat wheel sounds) are heard by both teams, increasing the chance of random or unjustified reports. 4. Even harmless or positive chat messages (e.g., “Good game, well played”) can trigger false reports. 5. This creates a negative experience for players who legally buy and use in-game content. I also want to share that I have many more ideas and suggestions on how to improve and fix certain aspects of the game, making both the player experience and the administrative work much easier. I would be more than happy if the Valve Support Team could contact me directly for a potential collaboration or partnership, in the name of keeping Dota 2 a safe, fair, and friendly place for everyone. Contact details: Email - justszaremba@outlook.com Thank you, Justs Zaremba

title: Please Review Behavior Score System – Years of Dedication Undermined
body: Hello Developers, I want to raise my frustration with the current Behavior Score system in Dota 2. I’ve been playing for over 13 years, and I’ve also invested a lot in cosmetics and supporting the game. Despite this, I feel the Behavior Score system unfairly punishes me. Here’s what I’ve noticed: I often receive commendations after games, yet my score still drops. A single report from a frustrated teammate seems to outweigh multiple positive commendations. Years of investment and effort can be overshadowed by an algorithm that doesn’t reflect my actual gameplay or sportsmanship. I try my best every game, but the system feels inconsistent and discouraging. I ask that you: Reconsider how reports vs. commendations affect the score. Review my own Behavior Score, which I believe does not reflect my true conduct in matches. Consider adjustments so players who are long-term positive contributors to the game aren’t penalized unfairly. I know Dota 2 is “just a game,” but for me and many others it’s a big part of our lives. I want to see the system improved so players like me can enjoy fair matchmaking and recognition for good behavior. Thank you for your time, and I hope the team can give this some serious attention.

title: The report system in Dota 2 is broken
body: ### Description Please stop counting player reports in winning games, or at least make it so they don’t affect accounts with already very low behavior scores, because this makes it impossible to climb out of this pit. In my Steam statistics, where reports are listed, it says that in the last 15 games I received reports in 7 of them, which should normally be given only for intentionally ruining games. But the thing is, I actually won most of those last 15 games. My behavior score was already extremely low (3383), and after these last 15 games it dropped to 2229, and now I can’t even find a ranked match. From my match history statistics it’s absolutely clear that I tried to win every single one of those 15 games, and the punishment I received is completely unfair. In the past week, I even ranked up 3 tiers, from Legend 5 to Ancient 3. Players report me either out of spite or as a joke, but I definitely never intentionally lost matches or interfered with others playing. I absolutely don’t understand why, despite putting in maximum effort in each of these last 15 games, I’m being punished. I was simply playing and wanted to win every single one of them, nothing more. I know at least three people who were forced to stop playing Dota because once they fell into the low behavior score “pit,” it became absolutely impossible to get out. Yes, they often ended up there partly through their own fault, myself included due to excessive match abandons, but this system doesn’t give any chance for redemption, even if you try 100%, as my example shows. And the funniest part is that the game after which I got a conduct penalty, at the end of it, the same people who clearly bombarded me with reports in the game all gave me a like—all four of them—but alas, the system is so “wonderful” that it means nothing. I just want to play, that's all, and now even my matchmaking button is blocked - this has to be a joke. ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) 8462043152 ### Screenshots

title: Behavior Score and the point of no return. #BehaviorScore
body: Every day in every Dota community there are several people complaining about this. I'm going to try to put into written words the voices of this group that still loves the game and doesn't want to give it up. I have over 25,000 hours of Dota 2 so I know the importance and the difference of having a good score. I Have immortal rank 5600MMR. Reports have become an additional skill within the game. People use them as if they were their hero's ability to attack others. We believe that infinite reports should be removed as soon as possible. In our opinion, the best way to STOP abuse would be to change the system. In Dota 2, a small detail changed in a patch can change the entire meta. Just as details make a difference within Dota 2's mechanics the endless reports are being abused to the detriment of players like us. We're calm and polite, but our conduct is unfairly reduced. This abuse, combined with an extremely competitive landscape, makes reports almost like real-life PvP skills. Furthermore, the system itself is our enemy, as I can see from the image below, I only earned 200 points in 15 matches with zero reports. [[ ]( That's very little it could be more. This would further encourage players to strive to receive even fewer reports. Many people are trying to improve their behavioral scores but are not succeeding even after trying for over a year and playing several games a day! But, the score just dropped. It is broken. To solve the main problem, we will point out some suggestions below that in our point of view would minimize/end these problems. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 1 - Immediate/provisional solution: Allow the Reset of conduct and communication scores with a Cooldown of 1 year, for example. and/or 2 - Long term solutions/balance: These infinite reports need to be better analyzed before they influence someone's behavioral score. and/or 3 - Option to schedule ranked matches with mandatory pause in case of disconnection of any player for up to 6 minutes. and/or 4 - Disconnecting may have a much smaller impact than currently practiced in reducing the behavior score and the communication scores. and/or 5 - Limit the number of reports. and/or 6 - Do not allow the accumulation of group reports (If a group of three people reports someone only one of those three reports should be considered randomly to prevent and punish fraud). and/or 7 - Reduce the minimum/maximum amount of behavior that is possible to lose in all situations by 50%. 8 -We welcome the participation of anyone suffering from system imbalances. Share your thoughts.

title: Feedback & Suggestions: Dota 2 Report and Behaviour System
body: ### Description # Feedback & Suggestions: Dota 2 Report and Behaviour System The current Dota 2 report and behaviour system feels unfair and easily exploitable, especially for players with behaviour scores below 6,000. Here are the main issues and suggestions: ## Issues Observed - **Difficulty Recovering Behaviour Score:** Once a player drops below 6k behaviour, it becomes nearly impossible to recover, even with consistently positive gameplay. - **Unfair Reporting:** Players often get reported despite carrying games and maintaining good conduct, sometimes simply for being muted or for no clear reason. - **Lack of Action Against Real Trolls:** Players who intentionally ruin games (e.g., staying in the jungle AFK for 20+ minutes in Turbo) rarely get banned, which encourages toxic behaviours. - **Abuse of Reporting:** Many players report anyone who is muted or disagrees with them, regardless of actual behaviour or performance. This creates a cycle of mass reporting. ## Suggestions for Improvement 1. **Limit Reports:** Remove infinite reports; instead, allow only one report per played match. 2. **Restrict Reporting from Toxic Players:** Players who have been recently reported should temporarily lose the ability to report others. 3. **Automate Warnings & Low Priority:** Automatically place players who remain AFK in the jungle or refuse to help their team into low priority after repeated offenses. 4. **Incentivize Cooperation:** Add incentives for positive teamplay and show behavioural/skill improvements after every match. 5. **Preserve Communication:** Do not remove communication entirely; allow players to choose who to mute, as teamwork is essential in Dota 2. 6. **Improve Reporting System Moderation:** The current automated reporting system is unfair. Introduce some form of AI review or at least human moderation to validate reports and prevent abuse. **Summary:** The current system punishes the wrong players and emboldens toxic behaviour. A few targeted changes could make the experience fairer and more enjoyable for everyone. Thank you for considering these suggestions! ```` ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) _No response_ ### Screenshots _No response_

title: Behaviour System Reset | Recalibration
body: Once a player's behavior score drops below 3000, it becomes nearly impossible to recover or recalibrate. At this level, communication with teammates is severely hindered, and the environment becomes increasingly toxic. Many players in this bracket show little respect for the game or their fellow players, often resorting to false or retaliatory reports. This creates a vicious cycle where even positive gameplay and genuine attempts to improve are overshadowed by constant reporting, keeping players trapped in this low-score bucket indefinitely. A system that allows for meaningful recovery or recalibration is desperately needed to break this cycle and encourage better behavior.![Image](

Matchmaking Settings: I have tried with "Strict Solo Queue" both enabled and disabled, and I selected all roles in the role queue. Timing: I have attempted to search for matches at different times, including peak hours in my region and other regions Steps I have already taken to try to resolve the issue: Verified the integrity of the game files through Steam. Restarted the Steam client and Dota 2 multiple times. Confirmed that my internet connection is stable (no ping or latency issues). body: ### Description Dear Dota 2 Support Team, I am reaching out regarding the recent ban on my Dota 2 account, as I am unsure about the specific reasons behind it and would greatly appreciate more details. Here’s an outline of my situation: Intent to Play Fairly: I am a dedicated player who strives to follow all guidelines and respect other players. I don’t use any prohibited software, scripts, or engage in any behavior that would harm other players’ experiences. Account Circumstances: Over the years, I’ve had multiple accounts due to challenges retrieving access to my main account. I also had to change my phone number, which may have contributed to confusion regarding account identity. My family shares a computer, and each family member has their own account. We log in separately, but this might have been flagged as suspicious activity. Desire to Follow Community Guidelines: If my actions were unintentionally perceived as smurfing, I’d like to better understand how I can adjust my behavior to avoid these misunderstandings. I want to continue playing within the game’s rules, as I am genuinely passionate about Dota 2. Questions for Clarification: Could you specify what actions led to this ban? How can I avoid these issues in the future, especially with shared computer usage in my household? Is there a possibility of reviewing this ban in light of the context provided? I appreciate any assistance you can offer, as my goal is to continue enjoying and supporting Dota 2 while adhering to all rules. I hope this information clarifies my intentions and circumstances. title: Behavior system needs an overhaul
body: ### Description Behavior score currently matters more than skill ranking on game quality experience and it probably will be the cause for many players to stop once the novelty of updates wears off. **The report is both underutilized and abused.** My guess is most people dont actually bother reporting, they either dont know the options exist or its not intuitive to get to that page. Why do I say this? because 2-3 reports from 2 parties can land you in LP with NO OVERWATCH ASSESSMENT (the assessment occurs before the replay is even available for download). Think about that, out of 135 players you encounter in 15 matches that could report you, 2-3 reports is not even 2%. Not to mention Im talking from experience in TURBO mode, not ranked, not even casual AP. Suggestion#1: If commend worth was decreased to prevent players form boosting BS through turbo, then also adjust the weight of reports, particularly when it comes to dashing out punishment. Currently a conduct update with 30+ commend and reports nets around 150-180 BS. So if a player DCs or abandons you are telling that player that they need to play ~100 games to recover. That to me does not seem balanced at all. (I have no doubts overwatch eventually will be partly AI powered, it needs to a account when losses are simply stomps, and I cant emphasize this enough, an ability draft or turbo game is much different than All pick or ranked, they cant be treated the same) Suggestion#2: Baselines for behavior should be aligned with average BS, lower BS players tend to be a lot more trigger happy with report use, while top BS players might not bother reporting at all. The same behavior in a lower BS match can net you reports you wouldn't get at high BS. Since you are allowing players with questionable behavior to make the call I think its only fair that their report is curved appropriately. **Reports are not being used correctly,** from overwatch reviews about 50% of them I see no griefing behavior, people report players they dont like more often than behavior that should be punished, and the way devs have limited this is to give each player limited reports. Also this affects new players, Ive had several friends I tried to introduce to the game get reported for griefing when they were just learning the game. Losing or getting stomped or even underperforming are not valid reasons to be called a griefer or get reported, the system currently takes no account of this **Suggestion#3:** Make reports actually be submitted at the END of the match, when people have cooler heads, when players that quit 3 minutes before the game ends have already closed the game. This prevents people from assessing what went on in the match entirely instead of an instance of someone rage buying back, or a player with a unconventional pick or build. They can still flag instances of behavior during the match, although since about a year ago you can no longer report a player multiple times a match to flag when they were being toxic, so I am guessing the devs saw no value in this **Suggestion#4:** Instead of giving the option to a player to click every single box in the report page, make players select a single reason per report through a tickbox or dropdown menu UI. Lists what constitutes and what does not constitute griefing, comm abuse, hacking, scripting, etc. CS2, Apex, overwatch and many other online comp games use this players that actively engage in repeat griefing should not be able to report. I would even say it doesnt make sense for a player that went 0-35 feeding mid in a game to have the power to report anyone else in that game, and I can confirm Ive been at the receiving end of this. **Suggestion#5:** Dont allow repeat offenders to use reports, even retroacrtively remove reports they have submitted if they are found guilty of bad behavior in the same match. These players would need a clear statement of the consequence to their actions. Give them feedback that they temporarily lose the ability to call out other players behavior because of their own. **Suggestion#6:** Immortal behavior is probably at its worst with the current drafting system. It seems to give a pass to players to be toxic because they are at the top 5% of rank jsut so that queue times arent as long. All this is doing is encouraging players to purchase alt accounts to play in or resort to boosting services. Make example of players, example, Mason Ona final note, If the goal of the devs is to get people in a treadmill run of BS farming, you will lose player base once the novelty of updates wear off. What keeps dota players coming back and not quitting is match quality. The suggestions I put forward go along with the current system, I think a much bigger overhaul (like allowing infinite reports like in CS and re-baselining automatic punishment) and simplifying the system would only improve player experience, but at least are small things that could help. I hope some attention is brought on this matter ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) _No response_ ### Screenshots _No response_

title: Behavior score - Overly sensitive in Turbo mode?
body: ### Behavior Score/Conduct Summary excessively brutal drops in score TLDR: I believe there must be some sort of integer error affecting the conduct summary and behavior score system. I provided data documenting my personal conduct summary numbers from Steam's Personal Game Data page. Preamble: I have been playing Turbo mode in order to try to raise my behavior score. This failed miserably as evidenced by the current behavior score of 1. I have been punished by the Overwatch system multiple times with bans and low priority. I do not believe I have been acting in a way in game to warrant, especially in turbo games where it's supposed to be a casual mode for fun, and yet the amount of reports is insanely high from the players. Some of these conduct summaries were generated on the same day, either by actually playing 15 games in a day, or it auto-triggered and decreased score and gave me low priority. Again, I have been treating turbo games as a job, working to raise the score and have submitted requests to steam support about this. They have directed me to open a ticket here. Request: Please look at the data and see if there are any outstanding irregularities which would contribute to such a rapid decrease in score. I have a few questions to interpret from the data. Why is there a negative integer? -34 and -67 reports Why am i losing more score between summaries where more games were marked "positive" than not? Why do i not gain score where there are 2 matches reported by 6 players compared to gaining score 27 reports by 12 players? These summaries are classified as Periodic and not Excessive Reports. Is it statistically relevant to have so many commends and so many reports in the same conduct summary? It has been a long-standing theory of mine that commends do not affect score, but if they are somehow not being counted then. Are communication abuse reports being counted when below 3000 score and pings and voicelines are rate-limited to once every 60 seconds? Why? What about below 6000 score when you can use voicelines but not text chat? Is this counted as negative communication? What about below 7000 score, are multiple pings with a communication abuse report being triggered as a true positive? Why in God's name if yes? I have included 4 screenshots that valve can decipher the Unix time of where patch 7.33 begins and where the change was made to the behavior score. It is my theory the system was reverted a few weeks after implementation, because people were. During this period, I personally had no complaints and thought my game quality was acceptable. I reached 5000 MMR for the first time during this period. I am currently banned from Ranked. The screenshots are of the personal game data accessible on (For anyone reading this who would like to see their own game data, please replace my Steam user number in the link with your own. Follow Account -> Incoming Match Player Report.) The column dates of course are organized from most recent to latest. I will be following the thread closely, please do add your thoughts if you have any comments about my data. Thank you. ### Example Match ID: 7423620413 In the last turbo game I played before I was issued an automated 24 hour ban + at this time unknown number of low priority games, and a 1299 drop in behavior score to 1. I was matched with a party of 4, who took it upon themselves to grief and scapegoat me, as well as report me. I reported them and all 4 heros showed up as "action taken". It was easy to tell since I didn't report any other players. At 12 minutes Magnus wrote in the chat he was done. At around 15-16 min Magnus wasted RP in our fountain, used refresher, and wasted RP again. The game was over at 17 min, but I believe we could have won if the party of 4 did not give up. my dotabuff: ### Screenshots the ridiculously slow climb begins. I have been assessed a 24 hour ban and X games of low priority, as well as an instant reduction in 400 points after losing a game in which my teammates played less than average and exhibited toxic behavior. The automated system is a mistake, the report system is a mistake, trusting Valve gives a rat's ass about actual players is a mistake. I have decided to add some more pages of my history to demonstrate, while i never managed to remain at a high 10k score, my behavior was well above the range that i find myself trapped at now.

title: Toxic Players Artificially Boosting Behaviour Score
body: ### Description Ever since the change to the behaviour score system, every game I play has been filled with toxic players who possess artificially inflated behaviour scores. The loading animation that plays immediately after the drafting phase always features a player who has received 120+ commends in the past few games, which is of course impossible unless every player on both teams is commending them after every game they play. Given that these individuals are often muted or proceed to conduct themselves in such a way as to warrant a mute or a handful of griefing reports, it is obvious that these players deserve low behaviour scores but are participating in some sort of lobby system in which the 9 other players in the lobby are commending them after each game. I'm not exactly sure how it works, but I can't think of any other explanation. This has resulted in a far worse matchmaking experience than the one I had prior to the behaviour score change. I have a very high behaviour score, but my games are now filled with the sorts of toxic, game-ruining players I never had to play with under the old system. When I first read the changelogs, I thought the new system would be fantastic, and it certainly is on paper, but this artificial boosting needs to be fixed somehow so the changes can be positively felt as they were intended to be. ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) _No response_ ### Screenshots _No response_

title: Conduct summary needs better wording
body: Here's what a conduct summary currently looks like:![image]( Here's the tooltip associated with the behavior score:![image]( The problem (which I've seen people run into again and again) is that this screen implies two things it probably shouldn't: 1. The layout and lack of any explanatory text saying otherwise implies that behavior score is a direct function of the numbers shown below it and nothing else. 2. The tooltip reinforces this incorrect interpretation by implying that playing a match where you don't get reported is the one and only way to increase your behavior score. Now, I don't have any kind of internal knowledge on how behavior scores are calculated, but from screenshots posted by people complaining I can clearly see that the two assumptions are both incorrect. Coupled with @vMcJohn's excellent GDC presentation about implementing VACnet for CS:GO, which didn't reveal the formula for Trust Factor, but did say that it is not solely based on a player's in-game actions. An example given in the presentation was that a player was complaining about cheaters in their matches and it turned out the player had 50 closely associated accounts that had been VAC banned. I've seen people on the Dota 2 forum complaining that they created a smurf account and their behavior score followed them and even decreased further, so there's definitely something similar going on (or the behavior score system is just ridiculously good at guessing intent). --- With all that said, my suggestion is a simple one: add one additional sentence to the conduct summary, reading: > Your behavior score is not solely determined by the numbers on this screen.

body: ### Description Before I reached 100 hours of play time in normal matches, I wasn't penalized in the Overwatch system or given low priority games. In ranked games I have an average of 50-55% win rate, I don't spoil the game for other players, I play in my support positions (4 or 5), I don't say a single sound in the last ~40 matches, I don't write a single word in chat, but I still get complaints from other players in the Overwatch system. I don't know what to do and why I am punished all the time. All this was not before the opening of rating matches. What should I do if I do not communicate with anyone, do not insult anyone, do not interfere with the game of other players, and do not intentionally lose? title: The "Conduct Summary" tool does not work correctly on my Dota 2 account
body: This is something that I have been seeing for a year or so, although I always excused it by saying that it would be something that was beyond my understanding; but it has reached a point where I have no doubt... the "Conduct Summary" tool does not work correctly on my Dota 2 account. I have compared my "Conduct Summaries" with those of many colleagues in recent months, and most of them have worse summaries than mine. While they manage to reach a "Conduct" level of 10,000 and maintain it without many issues, mine keeps dropping and fluctuating, and for about a year now, I haven't come anywhere close to a "Conduct" score of 10,000. It is true that I went through a phase where I complained about other people in chat, but that happened years ago. In the past few months, during which I've been conducting tests, I haven't even used the chat. I don't write or say anything negative to anyone; I always focus on my team and help everyone, especially since I usually play as an Off-Support or Hard Support because my preferred position of Hard Carry is already taken in 99% of the matches. I don't want to spend 30 minutes in the queue ¬¬'. I am consistently recognized as a "Featured Player" in 87% of my matches, and I am even the MvP in almost 35% of them. I NEVER receive any reports of any kind, yet my "Conduct" score keeps decreasing and moving without being able to increase. Sometimes, I receive +20 positive comments and no reports, but my "Conduct" score only goes up by 50 points or even drops by 100 points ¬¬'. It makes no sense at all. To make matters worse, sometimes my "Conduct Summary" updates more than once in the same day without having played or even come close to 15 matches between summaries, and this is something you will see in some of the screenshots I will upload. This is not normal, it makes no sense, and I request a review of my account. A review that Steam itself has already denied, attributing everything to the fact that "Behavior Summaries" are generated automatically... as if being "automated" makes it perfect and devoid of any issues. When did humans give so much power to technology that they don't even bother to check for irregularities? Have we gone mad, or stupid, or something worse... useless? I want my account to be reviewed because what I'm experiencing is far from normal. And I want to point out that I have seen dozens of people facing the same issue, complaining since 2019 without receiving any help or support from Valve, which is lamentable for a company of its size. title: macOS][Apple M2] Dota 2 crashes 2–5 minutes into gameplay — EXC_GUARD / GUARD_TYPE_MACH_PORT
body: I'm experiencing persistent Dota 2 crashes on my MacBook Pro M2. The game launches successfully, and I can enter a match normally. However, after approximately 2–5 minutes of gameplay, Dota 2 unexpectedly crashes. The issue prevents me from playing matches reliably. System information - Device: MacBook Pro with Apple M2 - Hardware model: Mac14,7 - Operating system: macOS 26.6.2 (25G83) - Architecture: x86-64 (translated through Rosetta 2) - Graphics renderer shown in crash report: Vulkan via MoltenVK - System Integrity Protection: Enabled - Game: Dota 2 through Steam Steps to reproduce 1. Launch Steam on macOS. 2. Open Dota 2. 3. Enter a match. 4. Play normally for approximately 2–5 minutes. 5. Dota 2 unexpectedly crashes. Troubleshooting attempted - Enabled the Dota 2 developer console. - Attempted the `tv_stop true` workaround. - Tested gameplay again. - The game continues to crash. Crash report details ```text Process: dota2 Identifier: com.valvesoftware.dota2 Code Type: X86-64 (Translated) OS Version: macOS 26.6.2 (25G83) Exception Type: EXC_GUARD Exception Subtype: GUARD_TYPE_MACH_PORT Exception Message: INVALID_OPTIONS on mach port 0 Exception Codes: 0x0000000009c00000 0x8001430200000003 Termination Reason: Namespace GUARD Code 2305843022098595840 Triggered by Thread: 4 Thread 4: google_breakpad::ForwardException google_breakpad::ExceptionHandler::WaitForMessage Error Formulating Crash Report: RIP register does not match crashing frame ``` The crash report indicates that Valve's Breakpad exception handler encounters a Mach port guard violation. This may be masking an earlier crash within the game. The report also shows an active `HLTVServerAsync` thread, although I cannot confirm whether it contributes to the failure. Expected behavior Dota 2 should remain stable throughout matches on supported macOS systems. ### Actual behavior The game terminates unexpectedly after approximately 2–5 minutes of gameplay. Related issues - ValveSoftware/Dota2-Gameplay#34038 - ValveSoftware/Dota-2#3445 Request Please investigate this recurring gameplay crash affecting Dota 2 on Apple Silicon Macs running through Rosetta 2. I have the full macOS crash report available and can provide additional logs if necessary. Thank you.

title: Socketing a tradable Prismatic Gem into a non-tradable Arcana permanently and silently makes the gem non-tradable/non-marketable, with no warning given
body: ### Description Description: When a tradable/marketable Prismatic Gem (purchased via Steam Community Market with real money) is socketed into a non-tradable item (such as an Arcana received from a Battle Pass / Swag Bag), and later removed from that item, the gem permanently inherits the "Not Tradable / Not Marketable" restriction from the host item. The core issue: At no point during the socketing process, nor during the extraction/removal process, is the user given any warning that this action will permanently revoke the tradable/marketable status of their own separately purchased item. This results in real financial loss for players who paid real money for these gems, with no way to reverse the outcome. Steps to reproduce: Purchase a Prismatic Gem via Steam Community Market (tradable/marketable). Socket the gem into an Arcana that is itself non-tradable (e.g., received from a Battle Pass/Swag Bag). Later, use an Artificer's Hammer to destroy/recycle the Arcana in order to retrieve the gem. Observe that the extracted gem is now permanently marked "Not Tradable / Not Marketable," despite being fully tradable before this process. Expected behavior: Either: The gem should retain its original tradable/marketable status after being removed from a non-tradable item, since it was never part of the free/non-tradable item itself, OR At minimum, a clear and explicit warning should be shown before socketing or before destruction, specifically informing the user that their own paid item will become permanently non-tradable/non-marketable as a result. Actual behavior: The gem becomes permanently non-tradable/non-marketable with zero warning or disclosure at any step of the process, resulting in a loss of real monetary value for the user with no way to reverse the action. Additional context: I contacted Steam Support regarding this issue and was informed that this is "by design" and cannot be changed through support channels, and was advised to report this here instead, as a gameplay/system design issue. ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) _No response_ ### Screenshots

Missing Legacy Key for the new hero The newly added hero does not appear to have a proper Legacy Key assignment for the abilities. Players who use Legacy Keys have to manually work around the missing key assignments, which makes it difficult to use the hero with the same control setup as other heroes. Please consider adding a proper Legacy Key configuration for the new hero. 2. Quick Cast + Legacy Keys are not working correctly Recently, Quick Cast has stopped working properly when Legacy Keys are enabled. I normally use Legacy Keys together with Quick Cast, but now the combination does not behave as it used to. This makes the control setup especially difficult for players who have been using Legacy Keys for a long time. The issue appears to be related specifically to the interaction between Legacy Keys and Quick Cast, rather than Quick Cast itself. Expected behavior When Legacy Keys are enabled, each ability should have its corresponding Legacy Key, and Quick Cast should activate the ability immediately when the assigned key is pressed, just as it does with the normal keybind system. Actual behavior The new hero does not have a proper Legacy Key assignment. Quick Cast does not work correctly with Legacy Keys. This makes it difficult or impossible to use the new hero with the same Legacy Key + Quick Cast setup that players have used previously. Please investigate whether there was a recent change that affected the interaction between Legacy Keys and Quick Cast. I would really appreciate it if the Legacy Key assignments for the new hero could be added and the Quick Cast + Legacy Keys behavior could be restored to how it worked previously. Thank you for your work on Dota 2. title: False Overwatch conviction — Patrol found me guilty without identifying any violation
body: ### Ability name DEVASTATION ### Description Hello Valve, I would like to report what I believe is an incorrect Overwatch / Patrol conviction on my account. On August 29, 2026, I received an in-game notification saying: "After a recent game, the Overwatch service found you guilty of a violation." I do not understand what violation I supposedly committed and I strongly disagree with the verdict. Here is my recent match history from August 29: 20:54 — Tidehunter — WIN — 22:44 20:30 — Tiny — WIN — 16:31 20:03 — Razor — WIN — 14:00 19:22 — Shadow Fiend — LOSS — 28:54 All of these matches were Turbo games. As you can see, immediately before receiving the Overwatch conviction I played several matches normally, including three consecutive wins. I did not intentionally grief, feed, go AFK, destroy my items, abandon a match, or deliberately sabotage my team. If I made a mistake during a match, that should not automatically be considered intentional griefing. The main problem is that the Patrol notification provides absolutely no useful information about the alleged violation. I am not told: - Which Match ID was reviewed. - Which exact match resulted in the conviction. - What exact action was considered a violation. - At what timestamp the alleged violation happened. - What type of violation I was found guilty of. - What evidence the Patrol reviewers used. - How I can appeal an incorrect Patrol decision. I understand the purpose of Overwatch and I support using it against players who genuinely ruin games. However, an Overwatch system is only useful if its verdicts are accurate. Players can report others simply because they lost, disliked a hero pick, disagreed with an item build, disliked someone's playstyle, or were frustrated with their teammates. A player making mistakes or having a bad game is not the same thing as intentionally griefing. In my case, I believe the Patrol made an incorrect decision and I would like Valve to investigate it. Please provide or internally verify: 1. The Match ID that was reviewed. 2. The exact category of violation. 3. The timestamp(s) of the alleged violation. 4. The gameplay evidence that justified the guilty verdict. 5. Whether the verdict was based on actual gameplay evidence rather than simply the number of reports. 6. Whether this Overwatch conviction can be reviewed if the verdict was incorrect. I am not asking Valve to blindly remove a legitimate punishment. If I actually violated a rule, I want to know exactly what I did and in which match. But if there was no intentional violation, then this is an example of a false Overwatch conviction and the resulting punishment should be reconsidered. Please investigate the case and the Overwatch/reporting system responsible for this verdict. Screenshot of the Patrol notification and recent match history are attached. Date of notification: August 29, 2026 Thank you. ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) 8972872540, 8972830756, 8872784878, 8972708120

title: Feedback on the new Ranked Role Queue system
body: Hello, Dota 2 Team. I would like to share feedback regarding the new Ranked matchmaking system after the latest update. I understand the goal of encouraging players to queue for all roles in order to reduce queue times and improve matchmaking. However, I believe the current implementation has the opposite effect on match quality. Previously, players had a choice. Those who preferred Ranked Roles could use them, while others could play Ranked Classic without role restrictions. Now, Ranked Roles are effectively the only option, and selecting preferred roles requires spending Role Queue Tokens that can only be earned by queuing for all roles. This creates several problems. First, many players are now forced to play roles they are neither comfortable with nor experienced on. For example, I mainly play ranged heroes as Carry, Mid, or Support. I do not enjoy playing Offlane or tank heroes, and I have significantly less experience on that role. When the system assigns me Offlane simply because I need to earn Role Queue Tokens, the quality of my performance is naturally much lower. This is not about refusing to cooperate or wanting to play only one role. It is about recognizing that players have different strengths. A player with thousands of games on Carry will not suddenly become a good Offlaner because the matchmaking system assigned that role. As a result, everyone loses: * the player is frustrated because they cannot play the role they enjoy; * teammates receive a weaker performance than they expected; * overall match quality decreases. Some players may even feel pressured to ignore their assigned role and switch lanes, creating arguments before the game has properly started and increasing the number of role abuse reports. This is an unhealthy incentive created by the system itself. The previous system allowed players to decide whether they wanted to earn tokens by playing every role. The new system removes that freedom and makes it effectively mandatory for anyone who wants to continue selecting preferred roles consistently. I believe there are better alternatives, such as: * bringing back Ranked Classic as an option; * allowing players to earn Role Queue Tokens by selecting one or more high-demand roles instead of all five; * providing additional ways to earn tokens without forcing players into roles they do not know how to play. I truly appreciate the work that goes into improving Dota 2, and I understand that reducing queue times is important. However, I believe that match quality should remain the highest priority. A shorter queue is not necessarily an improvement if it results in players being forced into roles where they cannot perform at their best. Thank you for taking the time to read this feedback.

title: Feedback on the Overwatch and Behavior System, false reports.
body: ### Description I've been playing Dota 2 for many years, and I appreciate the effort Valve has put into improving the game. However, I believe there is an important issue with the current Overwatch and behavior systems that deserves attention. My main concern is that Overwatch reviewers may not always have enough context to accurately judge a player's actions. A single moment in a match can look like griefing without showing everything that happened beforehand. Sometimes a player is reacting to teammates who have been AFK farming, refusing to join fights, abandoning their role, or otherwise making the game extremely difficult to play. Without seeing the full progression of the match, it's easy to misinterpret those situations. I also think reports after a loss can sometimes be driven by frustration rather than actual griefing. If several players report someone simply because they lost, that player may repeatedly end up in the review system even if they were trying to win. I'm not saying the behavior system should be removed. I believe it is necessary. However, I think it could be improved by giving reviewers more context before making a decision and by continuing to refine how reports are evaluated. Some ideas that might help are: Allow reviewers to watch more of the match before and after the reported incident. Provide better timeline context for important events. Continue improving the detection of false or frustration-based reports. Ensure that players who consistently grief games are identified accurately while players who are genuinely trying to win are not punished unfairly. I enjoy Dota 2 and want the system to be as fair and accurate as possible. I hope this feedback is helpful and can contribute to future improvements. I can provide game id`s if necesary. title: Dota 2 freezes on startup when launched from Steam after 27 June 2026 update
body: Summary After the latest Dota 2 update (27 June 2026), Dota 2 consistently freezes on the black startup screen with the Dota logo only when launched through Steam. System Windows 10 22H2 (Build 19045) AMD Ryzen 5 2600X NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1060 3GB 16 GB RAM Latest NVIDIA driver (582.66, clean installation) Reproduction Open Steam. Click Play on Dota 2. Steam changes to Stop. Black screen with the Dota logo appears. dota2.exe becomes Not Responding and remains frozen indefinitely. The issue occurs every time. What works Launching dota2.exe directly from:...\steamapps\common\dota 2 beta\game\bin\win64\ starts the executable correctly (it then reaches the expected Valve Anti-Cheat check because it was not launched normally through Steam). This indicates the executable itself is capable of starting, while the freeze only occurs when using Steam's normal Play button. Troubleshooting already performed Verified game files. Completely reinstalled Dota 2. Rebuilt the Steam installation. Updated NVIDIA graphics drivers. Performed a clean NVIDIA driver installation. Reset Dota userdata (userdata\570). Disabled fullscreen optimizations. Confirmed compatibility mode and "Run as administrator" are disabled. Disabled overlays. Ran sfc /scannow (Windows repaired corrupted files). Restarted the PC. Freed significant disk space. Tested DirectX and Vulkan launch options. None of the above changed the behaviour. Debugging Using Process Explorer, the busiest thread while the game is frozen shows a stack including: engine2.dll resourcesystem.dll rendersystemdx11.dll!NVSDK_NGX_UpdateFeature dota2.exe!BSecureAllowed The renderer appears to begin initialization before the application hangs. Additional Information The issue started immediately after the 27 June 2026 update. Other Steam games launch and run normally. Windows Event Viewer records no application crash. The problem is fully reproducible on every launch.

title: Unclear Artificer's Hammer UI — "Destroy" Warning Does Not Distinguish Between Gem and Arcana, Leading to Accidental Loss of Limited Items
body: The confirmation prompt when using the Artificer's Hammer does not clearly distinguish between destroying an extracted gem and destroying the entire base item (including limited, account-bound Arcanas). This ambiguity causes players to accidentally delete irreplaceable items. Steps to Reproduce: Own an Arcana with a socketed gem. Purchase a new gem from the Community Market with the intent to swap it. Acquire an Artificer's Chisel. Use the Artificer's Hammer on the Arcana. Observe the confirmation prompt: it asks the player to type "destroy" but does not explicitly state that the Arcana itself will be permanently deleted. Expected Behavior: The confirmation prompt should clearly state: "This action will permanently delete [Item Name]" — if the entire item will be destroyed. "This action will only destroy the extracted gem" — if only the gem is being removed. Players should not be expected to infer which part of the item is being destroyed, especially when dealing with limited-edition, account-bound rewards. Actual Behavior: The current prompt is vague and uses the word "destroy" without specifying the target. Players who are new to the gem extraction mechanic — or who have never used it before — reasonably assume that "destroy" applies to the old gem being removed, not to the Arcana itself. Real Example (Evidence Attached): I am attaching a screenshot from my Steam Inventory History (December 9, 2022) that demonstrates this exact scenario: On Dec 8, I received the Fractal Horns of Inner Abysm (Terrorblade Arcana) from the TI11 Swag Bag. On Dec 9, I purchased a new gem (Kinetic: Prosperity Remnants) from the Community Market. I then acquired an Artificer's Chisel and used it on the Arcana. I believed the "destroy" confirmation was for the old gem. Instead, the entire Arcana was deleted. The inventory log does not even show a "Removed" entry — only "Socket added" twice. The item simply vanished without a clear deletion log. This proves the UI failed to communicate what was actually happening. Why This Matters: This bug cost me an account-bound, limited-time TI11 Swag Bag Arcana that is completely irreplaceable. I have no way to re-obtain this item through any in-game or market system. Other Dota 2 players have reported the exact same issue on community forums. Request: Please review the Artificer's Hammer confirmation prompt to ensure it clearly specifies what is being destroyed (gem vs. base item). Additionally, adding a "Destroyed Item" log entry to the inventory history after a successful Artificer's Hammer use would help players understand what just happened and provide clearer records. Thank you for your time and for considering this feedback.

title: OFFICIAL STATEMENT FROM THE CIS DOTA 2 COMMUNITY TO VALVE
body: ### Description Description We, representatives of the CIS Dota 2 community, as well as, in essence, a significant portion of the global Dota 2 player base, would like to formally express our deep concern regarding the current state of the game and its direction in recent years. Dota 2 has long been more than just a game for us - it is a competitive environment, a community, and a cultural phenomenon. However, many long-standing issues continue to negatively impact the player experience, and we believe they are not receiving the attention they deserve. Behavior Score System The current behavior score system is widely perceived as ineffective and, in many cases, unnecessary. Instead of improving match quality, it often creates frustration and imbalance. The system discourages communication between players, lacks fairness, and at times does not accurately reflect actual in-game behavior. As a result, it reduces overall enjoyment of the game. Ranked System The ranking system raises serious concerns. The gap between skill levels and MMR brackets is extremely large, making progression disproportionately difficult and time-consuming. For many players, ranking up requires an unrealistic investment of time, which reduces long-term engagement and motivation. Cheating and Fair Play One of the most critical issues is the growing presence of cheaters in public matches. This problem severely undermines competitive integrity. Many players believe that anti-cheat measures are insufficient and that enforcement actions are nearly nonexistent. A stronger and more transparent stance on fair play is urgently needed. Quality of Updates Recent updates are perceived as lacking depth, coherence, and clear direction. Changes often feel unfinished or disconnected from the needs of the community. This creates the impression that development is no longer guided by a clear vision for the game. Gameplay and Balance There is growing concern regarding the current gameplay direction and overall balance of the game. The meta is heavily dominated by aura-based items, which reduces strategic diversity and limits viable playstyles. Matches have shifted away from dynamic teamfights toward prolonged farming, making gameplay feel slower and less engaging. Additionally, the current comeback mechanics often lead to excessively long games, even in situations where one team has a clear advantage. Overall, there is a strong ощущение that player feedback is not being adequately considered, and that balance decisions are disconnected from the community’s expectations. Lack of Meaningful Events Over the past year, there has been a noticeable absence of engaging and memorable in-game events. Historically, events have played a key role in maintaining player interest and community enthusiasm. Their decline has led to a significant drop in overall engagement. Technical Issues, Bugs, and Server Stability There is growing concern regarding the overall technical condition of the game. Players frequently encounter bugs that remain unresolved for extended periods of time. In addition, server instability has become a recurring issue - matches can suffer from severe lag, sometimes lasting 30 minutes or more, directly impacting game outcomes and ruining the competitive experience. Furthermore, numerous visual and interface-related bugs reduce usability, negatively affecting play. Taken together, these issues create the impression of insufficient attention to the technical quality of the game. We are writing this not out of negativity, but out of genuine concern for the future of Dota 2. We believe in the game’s potential and its legacy, and we hope to see it thrive once again. We strongly urge greater transparency, closer communication with the community, and decisive action on the issues outlined above. Respectfully, The CIS Dota 2 Community Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) No response Screenshots No response ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) _No response_ ### Screenshots _No response_

title: Arcade Lobby Abuse: Bot-Created Empty Lobbies Inflating Popularity Listings
body: There appears to be widespread abuse in the Arcade lobby system where creators are using bots to generate multiple empty or near empty lobbies. This artificially inflates their customer game's visibility in the "Open Lobbies" list **Observed Behavior** - Many lobbies appear as 1/x (e.g. 1/4, 1/8, 1/24) across multiple servers - These lobbies remain idle and do not fill with real players - The pattern is repeated across different regions, suggesting automated creation - This pushes legitimate, organically populated lobbies further down the list **Expected Behavior** - Lobby listings should reflect genuine player activity - The system should discourage or prevent artificial inflation via bots **Impact** - Misleads players into joining inactive or dead lobbies - Reduces visibility for legitimate custom games - Degrades overall trust in the Arcade ecosystem **Suggested Solutions** - **Idle Lobby Timeout**- Automatically remove or deprioritize lobbies that remain at 1/x for a prolonged period. - **Bot Detection / Rate Limiting** - Limit how many lobbies a single account or IP can create within a time window. - **Sorting Adjustment** - Prioritize lobbies with higher player counts or recent join activity over newly created ones. - **Report System for Arcade Abuse** - Allow players to flag suspicious lobbies or creators for review.

title: Behavior Score System Creates a Downward Spiral With No Recovery Path
body: Hello Developer Team, I would like to raise a concern regarding the behavior score and Overwatch penalty system in Dota 2. Over a relatively short period, my behavior score dropped from above 8000 to around 1300. This seems to have been primarily due to Overwatch penalties, and the resulting system restrictions are making the game very difficult to play. At behavior scores below 3000, players cannot use chat, which suggests that the system is not primarily addressing communication toxicity. In my case, I also have not been intentionally griefing games—I always play matches to completion and try to win. One possible source of reports may be my playstyle. I occasionally choose to play jungle-oriented strategies. While some teammates may dislike this approach, it is a legitimate playstyle and in many games I end up contributing significantly or even carrying the match. The main issue is that once the behavior score drops significantly, it becomes extremely difficult to recover. The system starts to feel like a downward spiral with very limited opportunity for improvement. It might be helpful if the system allowed players a clearer path to recover their score, for example: * a periodic recalibration opportunity (e.g., once per year), or * mechanisms that allow behavior score to recover more effectively through consistently completed games without reports. I believe the goal of the behavior system is to improve the overall player experience, but in its current state it can make the game feel unplayable for players who fall too far below the threshold. Thank you for taking the time to review this feedback.

title: Player feedback (playing since 2004): Behavior Score and communication restrictions
body: Hello, I would like to share some observations about the current Behavior Score and communication restriction system in Dota 2. I have been playing Dota since the Dota Allstars era (around 2004) and was also active during the time of dota-league.com, one of the earlier community platforms that already implemented matchmaking, reporting systems, and moderation. Having played the game for more than 20 years with very few breaks, I have followed the evolution of its systems quite closely. This post is not meant as a complaint, but rather as long-term player feedback about some interactions in the current system that may produce unintended effects on player behavior and match quality. Dota 2 relies heavily on coordination and information exchange between players. During matches, players often need to communicate things such as ultimate cooldowns, teleport cooldowns, buyback availability, or the need to delay a fight until certain abilities are available. These kinds of details can strongly influence the outcome of fights and objectives. When players receive communication restrictions due to Behavior Score penalties, it becomes difficult to communicate this type of information. As a result, teammates may misinterpret certain decisions during a match. For example, a player might not join a fight because abilities are on cooldown, because the engagement is clearly lost, or because positioning or farming for the next objective is the safer decision. Without communication, these decisions can easily appear as intentional non-cooperation. Reports are typically submitted during or immediately after matches. At that point, it may not yet be clear whether a decision that appeared questionable during the game was actually strategically correct. For instance, refusing to follow a teammate into a lost engagement may look negative in the moment but can later turn out to be the correct macro decision for the team. Because reports happen immediately, they can sometimes reflect frustration in the moment rather than an objective evaluation of behavior. When communication is limited, players also cannot explain their reasoning during the match. This may increase misunderstandings and lead to additional reports. I understand that Valve likely uses background systems to evaluate report accuracy over time, but restricted communication may still contribute to a feedback loop where misunderstandings increase reports and reports further reduce communication. From earlier community-run systems such as dota-league.com, reporting mechanisms also existed. Those systems were simpler and largely player-driven, but they often focused on clearly disruptive behavior. They also included moderation steps such as report reviews, cooldowns, temporary bans, and bans for multi-accounting to prevent players from bypassing penalties. While the system itself was simpler, enforcement against multi-accounting made it harder to circumvent the intended penalties. In the current environment, creating new accounts is relatively easy. While I understand that Dota 2 already has safeguards such as restricting ranked access for new accounts and estimating player skill before calibration matches, multi-accounting can still occur. Experienced players creating additional accounts can result in skill imbalances in matches. This may cause frustration among teammates and indirectly lead to toxicity or reports even when the underlying cause is the match imbalance rather than individual behavior. Another observation that may indicate unintended incentives relates to Low Priority Single Draft matches. Interestingly, some players report that these matches can sometimes feel less tense or less toxic than normal ranked games, even though they are intended as a penalty environment. From personal experience, I sometimes find Low Priority Single Draft games more enjoyable than regular ranked games, which seems paradoxical. I also know players who intentionally try to receive reports in order to play in Low Priority because they perceive those matches as less stressful than the normal Single Draft queue. If players intentionally attempt to enter Low Priority to access a different match environment, this may suggest that the system is producing unintended incentives. At the same time, intentionally steering accounts into Low Priority may further distort matchmaking and player behavior. Over the many years I have played Dota, it felt at certain points that the overall match environment was more balanced and less toxic. As someone who has followed the game for more than two decades, I find some of these developments unfortunate and would simply appreciate if this type of long-term player feedback could be considered during future improvements to the behavior and reporting systems. Thank you for taking the time to read long-form feedback from long-term players, and thank you for continuing to support the development of Dota 2.

title: Behavior Score is cooked
body: ### Description Hi, I want to give real feedback about the Behavior Score system, because honestly it feels broken and unfair. In my recent match, two of my teammates started watching everything I did and criticizing every move I made. They were constantly commenting on where I go, what items I build, why I’m on this lane, why I’m not grouping — basically judging every decision I made. At the same time, they were making mistakes themselves and dying for no reason. Because of that, I started responding and explaining what I was doing. I explained that I was split pushing, controlling lanes, creating pressure, and playing the map the way my hero is supposed to. I also started making calls — telling when to back, when not to fight, when to reset, and how we could stabilize the game. I also pointed out their mistakes, like when they went mid and died for nothing after objectives were already gone. I wasn’t trying to attack them, I was trying to explain the situation and help us win. Some teammates actually started listening to my calls. Others kept insulting me and blaming me. But I kept playing, kept calling, and kept focusing on winning. Eventually, even during fights and arguments, the team followed the path and calls I was making. My strategy worked, and we won the game. But during the conflict, I received a chat restriction. And after the match, I received a 4-hour matchmaking ban and lost around 1000 Behavior Score. This is the main problem. It feels like if you speak, communicate, and try to lead, you become a target. People get angry, they blame you, they report you, and the system punishes you automatically without understanding what actually happened. This has happened more than once. Whenever I try to communicate, make calls, ping objectives, or help coordinate the team, I become the most visible person, and frustrated teammates use reports against me. So the system basically teaches you one thing: don’t talk, don’t communicate, don’t try to lead. Just stay silent if you want to protect your Behavior Score. But Dota 2 is a team game. Communication should be encouraged, not punished. And this is not just my personal problem. This issue is widespread in the community. Many large YouTube creators have talked about the Behavior Score system and its problems. Videos discussing this topic have hundreds of thousands of views and tens of thousands of likes. There are entire discussions and videos dedicated to how frustrating and unfair this system feels for players who try to communicate and lead. Right now it feels like the system punishes players who try to play properly and help their team, simply because other players get emotional and use reports as a weapon. I hope you can seriously review and improve this system, because right now it discourages teamwork instead of supporting it. title: Petition to Remove the Communication Score System from Dota 2
body: ### Description Addressee: Valve / Dota 2 Development Team We hereby request the complete removal of the Communication Score system from Dota 2 as a fundamentally flawed system that causes direct harm to match quality. This conclusion is not based on an isolated incident. It is the result of years of real-world use and extensive community feedback. Over the lifetime of Communication Score, thousands of forum threads have been created on Steam, consistently describing the same issues: lack of transparency, unpredictable penalties, and the absence of a reliable recovery mechanism. Core issues No validation of communication content The system relies on reports without validating the actual content of communication. It does not distinguish between toxicity, active gameplay coordination, and frequent but neutral communication. As a result, it punishes: new players asking questions, team leaders making calls, any highly visible or communicative player. Opaque and inconsistent report weighting Reports have an unclear and inconsistent impact. Multiple reports may have little effect, while in other cases a single report can cause a massive score drop without explanation. This makes the system non-transparent and unreliable. Punishment without causal connection Reports from opposing players can be applied even when no toxic communication occurred. Emotion-driven reports after a loss are not filtered or distinguished from legitimate cases. No functional recovery path Even after hundreds of matches with positive behavior, minimal reports, and many commendations, the Communication Score may: stagnate indefinitely; collapse within a few matches. This indicates the absence of a valid recovery endpoint. Direct damage to competitive integrity Automatic mutes: reduce match quality, break team coordination, directly affect win and loss outcomes. This is especially damaging in premade groups, where communication is the primary reason players group up. Any automatic communication restriction in such cases contradicts the purpose of team play. System redundancy Dota 2 already provides effective individual filtering tools such as mute and ignore. These tools allow players to manage their own experience without breaking match symmetry. Communication Score adds no unique value. Long-term degradation of communication After more than three years of use: toxicity has not been eliminated, meaningful team communication has largely disappeared. Players increasingly choose silence out of fear of reports, even when communication would improve gameplay. This trend is widely documented across the Steam community. Request For the reasons stated above, we request the complete removal of the Communication Score system from Dota 2 as a system that is: structurally irreparable, opaque and unpredictable, redundant, harmful to match quality and team-based gameplay. ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) _No response_ ### Screenshots _No response_

title: Rework the reporting and behavior score system - I can’t enjoy your game.
body: In Dota 2 there is an unlimited reporting system; this is no secret. Reports are needed so the game doesn’t turn into real hell. I agree with that. But your reporting system is the worst, for several reasons. First, it allows the most toxic people to simply ruin other players’ accounts even when those players did nothing wrong, because by default reports are automatically counted as a behavior score penalty. Every report from both allies and enemies reduces behavior score, specifically by 150 points. I agree that reports should reduce behavior score, but only if you actually behaved badly. If you were just playing the game, just trying to win and doing everything you could, not destroying items, not interfering with your teammates’ chances to win, simply consistently trying to win, why do reports damage your behavior score? You have an Overwatch system where reports are reviewed before sending someone to low priority. Why not make it so that only reports confirmed by an Overwatch reviewer as a real violation reduce behavior score? Make the penalty larger if that’s the goal. But I don’t understand why I should be punished for picking a hero that another player wanted, or a hero that someone simply doesn’t like - Techies, Tinker, Arc Warden. It should never have worked this way, and it doesn’t feel fair. I also know that in 2019, without warning anyone, you banned a huge number of people who had 1000 behavior score or less. So if you do that again, I will simply lose an account I played on for 13 years, invested over 2000 dollars into, and spent 25,000 hours on. You leave me no choice except to not play matchmaking at all. I don’t want to lose my account, at least because I can sell the items on it and get my money back. And none of you will ever warn people in advance that, for example, soon everyone with less than 1000 or 3000 behavior score will be banned, especially when that score was tanked by mass reports. Moreover, many of the reports I receive, as a streamer and as a Ukrainian, are based on nationality. Because of the Ukrainian flag in my guild and on my avatar. This should never be a reason for a report or a reason for losing behavior score. You give the users of this game a huge tool for repression and for pushing players out of your popular game. I don’t know a single game where, just to play normally and speak on the microphone, you have to spend an entire year playing silently, on support heroes, without a nickname, avatar, or guild. That’s worse than prison. What’s more, it feels as if you specifically punished me for spending money on items in your game, especially on those that can no longer be bought or transferred to other accounts. If I had never paid you a single cent, I could easily switch to another account and your broken behavior score system would never be a problem for me. But the problem is that I am genuinely a huge fan of your game. I created a thread here thanks to which Dota gained the ability to set custom hotkeys for the talent tree and attribute bonuses. My second thread is currently in the top 3 by likes in that GitHub discussion section. Why do you hate players who simply love your game so much? And about reports: often I get reported just for going to the wrong lane. For example, I always play position 4 supports, which means I should go to the offlane. But because in ranked mode reports fly for everything and even for nothing, and I can’t recover my behavior score there, I’m forced to play Turbo or Ability Draft. And there I’m forced to deal with parties of two or more players. And I hear this classic voice chat phrase: “we’re a party, go to another lane or we’ll all report you.” That means I can get 2 to 4 reports right at the start of the game just because I decided to be a support and practice my support role. I can be forced and told: you go mid, or you go position one. Sorry, I picked Wisp. How am I supposed to play mid or carry on Wisp? This is a choice without a choice. For losing mid or performing worse on position one, I will get my reports anyway. I would gladly press a button that launches only solo queue. I am a Dota 2 fan. I am also a developer of custom game modes in Dota 2, such as OLD DOTA and ALL HEROES PUDGE ALL ITEMS MOM. I would play only those, but even there I get no peace, because for some reason you don’t give custom game creators any option to create a mode on a stable client instead of an unstable one, your current Dota 2 version which can change at any moment. In Warcraft 3, I can launch a custom game made 23 years ago and play without bugs or crashes because it’s on a stable client. I really would like to stay in Dota in some form, but I don’t have infinite patience or infinite money to pay a custom game developer four or more times a year to fix critical bugs that appear in a custom mode solely because you regularly update the game client and have not created a stable Dota version for custom game developers. Yes, it would increase download size, but the custom mode would be playable for years without constant heavy maintenance. You have a huge and wonderful library of Dota 2 modes that haven’t worked properly for years. And this trend continues. I can’t stay in Dota in its current state. I tried playing on Faceit servers, but for some reason even there, in Captain’s Mode, it’s possible to ruin the game endlessly by spamming the “GG” phrase. Why is there no per person cooldown for it, like for pause, for example a 5 minute cooldown and three uses per game? Why can’t I even play normally there? Please fix this. I am probably one of the most loyal fans of this game. I have played 14,000 matches. But for the past year I haven’t been able to play anything except Battle Cups and Faceit League, where it’s still possible to constantly spam “GG” to ruin the game as much as possible.

title: Broken behavior system that even ai recognize as broken
body: ### Description this is what ai said about your stupid broken system Dota 2's behavior system is widely considered "broken" by players because it creates toxic matchmaking trenches, disproportionately punishes good players through malicious reports (especially in lower tiers), struggles to differentiate genuine griefing from disagreements or off-meta plays, and heavily penalizes communication/abandonments more than it rewards positive behavior, leading to frustratingly low scores and unfair match quality. Key issues include unlimited reports, the impact of reports in casual games (like Turbo) affecting Ranked, and an inability to climb out of low-score pools once there. Core Problems with the Behavior Score System: Abuse of Reports: Players can report teammates for minor infractions (losing roll, missing spells, bad plays), and these reports count heavily, even if unverified by Overwatch. The "Trench" Effect: Lower behavior scores lead to more reports from other low-score players, creating a cycle where it's extremely hard to climb out, even with good behavior. Disproportionate Penalties: A few bad games (or even just power outages/bad internet) can tank a score, while regaining points through commends or positive games is slow and difficult. Unfair Punishment for Communication: The Communication Score (Comms Score) is highly sensitive; arguments or frustration in 15% of games can drop it significantly, forcing mutes and hindering team play, while positive play yields few points. Lack of Differentiation: Reports from Turbo (casual) games carry the same weight as Ranked, leading to casual abuse. System Imbalance: Reports and abandons often feel weighted far more heavily than commends, making positive actions insufficient to offset negatives. Player Experiences & Frustrations: Players report losing thousands of points for technical issues or bad luck, feeling unfairly punished for issues beyond their control. Good players get stuck in low-score pools with genuinely toxic players (feeders, intentional griefers) because the system segregates them. Many feel the system doesn't encourage improvement but rather punishes mistakes or perceived lack of meta adherence. In essence, while intended to isolate toxic players, the current behavior system often punishes good players who have bad luck, experience technical issues, or get caught in cycles of malicious reporting, creating more frustration and a worse environment. ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) _No response_ ### Screenshots _No response_

title: The Behavior System Is Slowly Killing Dota — and It’s Time to Admit It
body: ### Description I’ve been playing Dota for years. I’ve seen it evolve, improve, and sometimes break. But what’s happening now with the Behavior and Communication Score system isn’t an evolution — it’s slow destruction. Right now, I’m communication-restricted. I literally can’t talk to my teammates at all. Which means I can’t even be toxic if I wanted to — there’s no way to do it. And yet, my score keeps dropping. If you check my recent matches, my stats are far better than most of my teammates’, and I still get punished. Why? Because someone can lose a lane, hit a report button, and the automated system will just believe them. That’s not fairness. That’s a machine judging human behavior with zero context. Valve keeps saying “the system is automated, we can’t change it.” But this system punishes normal players just for playing. You can literally get a report before the game even starts, or because you didn’t die with your team in a 5v5. How is that improving the quality of Dota’s community? And let’s be honest — the moment Valve stopped showing online player statistics right after the new behavior system was implemented… it said everything. People are quitting. Not because they hate Dota, but because they’re tired of being punished by a broken system that doesn’t understand human behavior. Half of my friends already stopped playing months ago for the same reason. And now I’m done too — until something actually changes. I’ll tell everyone I know who still plays to do the same, because at this point, continuing to play just tells Valve that everything’s fine. But it’s not fine. This system is pushing people away from a game they love. We don’t need hand-holding. We don’t need perfect matchmaking. We just want a fair system that understands the difference between genuine toxicity and normal, competitive gameplay. Until that happens, Dota will keep losing players — not because the game is bad, but because the system is. I love this game, and that’s exactly why I’m saying this. Sometimes, the only way to save something is to admit it’s in trouble. ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) _No response_ ### Screenshots _No response_

title: Communication Abuse reports (in Turbo mode) carry way too much weight since they do not get reviewed by an overwatch jury.
body: ### Description At the moment, when queuing exclusively for Turbo mode, you only gain 150 Comms Score points if you get a perfect summary (0 reports after 15 matches). In Normal mode/Ranked mode, you gain 300 Comms Score points if you get a perfect summary (0 reports after 15 matches). This is a mathematical error on Valve's part. For example, lets say you put aside 4 hours to play Dota on your day off from work. If you queue for Normal/Ranked AP, with each game lasting 60 minutes on average, that means you played 4 games. And with 9 other players in each of those games, that means you can potentially be reported by 36 trolls (worst case scenario). But... if you queued exclusively for Turbo mode during those 4 hours of Dota, that means you played 8 matches (with each game lasting 30 mins on average). Which means you could potentially be reported by 72 trolls (worst case scenario) compared to when queuing for Normal/Ranked mode. So if you're queuing exclusively for Turbo mode, not only are you only gaining half as many Comms points per summary (best case summary with 0 reports), you're also risking getting twice as many reports because you are playing twice as many matches compared to Normal/Ranked mode. So to put things right mathematically speaking, Valve needs to change the system so that Comms reports only count as half a report each (compared to Normal/Ranked mode). Or alternatively, allow Turbo mode players to gain the full 300 Comms Score points per perfect summary (15 matches with 0 reports). Otherwise, Turbo players risk their Comms score falling into deficit twice as fast as Normal/Ranked players. It's far too easy for trolls and bullies to throw Comms abuse reports at anyone they dislike and there is no consequence for illegitimate reports. Plus people have an unlimited amount of Comms reports to spam. This needs to change. ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) _No response_ ### Screenshots _No response_
